Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 15, verse 1:

The surah, as we see, opens with the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-tawfiqiyya), which we have said were recited by Jibril (peace be upon him) in this form, and which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) memorised and conveyed to us in this form (ﷺ). They were revealed first to a people who excelled in the language and were people of eloquence and clear expression, and we do not find any among them who denied them.

They are disjointed letters that are pronounced by the names of the letters, not by what they denote (musammayat). We know that every letter has a name (ism) and has a denoted form (musamma). So when we say or write the word "kataba" (he wrote), we place the letters kaf, ba' and ta' next to one another so that the word is as we pronounce or read it. This is said to be the denoted forms of the letters; as for the names of the letters, they are "kaf", "ba'" and "ta'". Only the learner knows the names of the letters, and therefore when you want to test someone in reading and writing, you say to him: "Spell out (tahajji) the letters of the word you are writing." If he pronounces the names of the letters, we know that he is proficient in reading and writing. This Qur'an, as we know, was revealed as a miracle (mu'jiz) for the Arabs, who excelled in the language and who held markets for it, like the exhibitions we hold for our advanced industries. Therefore, Allah the Exalted willed that the miracle of the final Messenger should come from the kind of thing in which they excelled. Had the miracle been of a kind other than what they excelled in and were not accustomed to, they would have said: "If we had learned this matter, we would have produced something surpassing it." The miracle of the Qur'an came to them from the very kind in which they excelled, in the Arabic language, and with the same vocabulary made up of the letters from which your words are made. What made the Qur'an a miracle is that the one who spoke it is the Creator and not a creature. In "Alif-Lam-Ra'" are the very raw materials from which you make your language.

This is some of what scholars have been able to glean from the openings of the surahs. We must know that Allah has secrets in His words. He, the Exalted, says: ﴿He it is who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are clear (muhkamat), they are the foundation of the Book, and others that are allegorical (mutashabihat). As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow what is allegorical in it, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation. But none knows its interpretation except Allah. And those firm in knowledge say: "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord." And none will be reminded except those of understanding.﴾ (Surah Al ʿImran, 7)

That is, the Qur'an contains clear verses (muhkamat), which are the verses of rulings (ayat al-ahkam) upon which reward and punishment are based. As for the allegorical verses (mutashabihat), they are like those verses with which some surahs begin; those in whose hearts is deviation ask: "What is their meaning?" They say this not seeking a meaning, but desiring discord.

To these we say: Do you wish to understand everything with your intellects? The intellect is only a means of perception, like the eye and the ear. Can your eyes see everything that can be seen? Of course not, because sight by the eye has laws and limits: if you are at a great distance from a thing you will not see it, for the eye does not see beyond the limit of the horizon.

Each person's horizon differs according to the strength of his sight: there is one whom Allah has blessed with strong and keen sight, and there is one who is weak-sighted and needs medical glasses to help him see clearly.

If the eye, which is the means of perceiving visible things, has limits, and if the ear, which is the means of perceiving sounds, has a limit set by the wave-distance of sound, then there must be limits to the intellect: it can understand what it can understand, and there is what it cannot understand. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the verses of the Qur'an: "What you know of it, act upon; and what is allegorical in it, believe in it." This is to safeguard the appointed times and dates of the birth of every secret hidden in the noble Qur'an; for if the Qur'an had given all its secrets in the first century in which it was revealed, how would it meet the subsequent centuries without a new secret?

Therefore: whenever the human intellect advances, Allah permits the unveiling of a secret of the secrets of the Qur'an. No one is able to dispute the verses of rulings. The Exalted says concerning the allegorical verses: ﴿None knows its interpretation except Allah, and those firm in knowledge say: "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord."﴾ (Surah Al ʿImran)

There are those who read this verse as follows: "None knows its interpretation except Allah and those firm in knowledge [wa-l-rasikhuna]..." and they forget that the utmost of being firm in knowledge is that you believe in those verses as they are.

The Exalted says: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra. These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an.﴾ (Surah Al-Hijr, 1)

"Tilka" (these) is a reference to what has preceded and what is yet to come of the Book, and "ayat" (verses) is the plural of "aya", which means: a wondrous thing to which attention is drawn. Verses are either cosmic, like night and day, the sun and the moon, to establish the Higher Existence; or they are the miraculous signs that testify to the truthfulness of the message from Allah, which are the miracles of the Messengers; or they are the verses of the Qur'an that carry the method for all mankind.

The Exalted adds: ﴿and a clear Qur'an﴾ (Surah Al-Hijr, 1)

Is "the Book" something other than the Qur'an? We say: when "al-kitab" is used without qualification, it refers to everything that Allah sent down to the Messengers, such as the scrolls of Ibrahim, the Psalms of Dawud, the Torah of Musa and the Gospel of Isa; all of these are books, and that is why they are called "the People of the Book" (ahl al-kitab).

But when the word "al-kitab" comes definite with the article "al-", it refers only to the Qur'an, because it was revealed as the final Book, and as a guardian (muhaymin) over the other books. Then He follows it with the particular description, which is "Qur'an", and thus He has coupled the specific with the general: "the Book" is the Qur'an. By this He indicates that it would be written as a book, and it was already written beforehand in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz).

If it is said: the earlier books were also written down; the answer is that those books were written down a long time after they were revealed, and they were not written the way the Qur'an was written at the moment of receiving it from Jibril (peace be upon him). The Qur'an is distinguished by having been written in the very time of its revelation, and it was not left for centuries as the rest of the books were, and then begun to be written.

The Qur'an is described as clear in itself and as making other things clear; and it also encompasses everything. The Exalted said: ﴿We have not neglected anything in the Book﴾ (Surah Al-An'am, 38).

Whatever matter requires a ruling, you will either find it detailed in the Qur'an, or we ask about it the people of remembrance (ahl al-dhikr), in confirmation of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿So ask the people of remembrance if you do not know﴾ (Surah Al-Anbiya', 7).

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 15 (al-Hijr), verse 2:

The word "rubba" (رب) is a particle used for paucity (al-taqlil), and it is also used for abundance (al-takthir), depending on what follows it. Its original usage is to precede a singular noun. We say "Rubba akhin laka lam taliduhu ummuk" ("Perhaps a brother of yours whom your mother did not bear"), which is for paucity, just as we say "Rubama yanjahu al-kasul" ("Perhaps the lazy one succeeds"). But if we say "Rubama yanjahu al-dhaki" ("Perhaps the intelligent one succeeds"), this is for abundance, and in this there is the use of a thing in its opposite, to awaken the intellect so that it pays attention. Here the Truth, glory be to Him, came with "rubba" together with "ma" and after them a verb. And it is shameful to say that "ma" here is superfluous, because the speaker is the Lord of all worlds. Here the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims﴾ (Surah al-Hijr 15:2). So will a time come when the people of disbelief wish that they had submitted? The verb "yawaddu" means "to love," "to incline toward," and "to wish," and everything you incline toward and wish for is called "talab" (request/demand).

It is said in the language: if you request a matter that may be realized, and may not be realized, then if you say, "Would that youth would return one day" (ya layta al-shabab ya'udu yawman), this is a request that cannot be realized; therefore it is said to be "tamanni" (wishing). And if you say, "Perhaps I will visit so-and-so" (la'alli azuru fulanan), this is called "raja'" (hoping), because it is possible for you to visit so-and-so. And you may say, "How many do you have?" intending to know the mental image of the one you ask, and this is called "istifham" (interrogation).

Thus, if you have requested something precious that cannot be attained, it is "tamanni"; if you have requested something that can be attained, it is "tarajji"; and if you have requested the image of a thing rather than its reality, it is "istifham." But if you request the reality of a thing, you are requesting it so that you do not do the act.

The request here in this verse says: ﴿Perhaps those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims﴾ (Surah al-Hijr 15:2).

So is this request possible?

Let us see when they will wish that. That wish will occur if events befall them that strip away their obstinacy, so that they weigh matters by true measures.

The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And they denied them, though their souls were convinced of them, out of injustice and arrogance﴾ (Surah al-Naml 27:14).

It happened to them when the battle of Badr took place and the Muslims took the spoils from them, that they said, "Would that we had been Muslims," and we took those spoils; that is, this wish occurred in this world, and it will occur at the death of each of them. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back. Perhaps I will do righteousness in what I have left behind"﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun 23:99–100).

The Truth, glory be to Him, comments on this statement: ﴿No! It is merely a word he is saying﴾ (Surah al-Mu'minun 23:100).

And they will also wish to be Muslims, in confirmation of the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him: ﴿If only you could see when the criminals hang their heads before their Lord, "Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so send us back; we will do righteousness; indeed, we are certain"﴾ (Surah al-Sajdah 32:12).

So there will come a time when the disbelievers wish they had been Muslims, when they witness something that strips away their denial and obstinacy, and it says to them: the life to which you clung is perishing; but you now ask to be Muslims at a time when obligation has ceased, and it is too late.

It suffices the Muslims as honor that they are upon the religion of God and have held fast to obligation, and it suffices you as shame that you have suffered this manifest loss and grieve that you were not Muslims.

On the Last Day, the Truth, glory be to Him, will punish the sinful Muslims who did not repent of their sins and did not seek forgiveness from the Truth, glory be to Him, or those whose sins He has not forgiven, due to lack of sincerity of intention and goodness of heart when seeking forgiveness. This includes the people of hypocrisy, in confirmation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times...﴾ (Surah al-Tawbah 9:80).

So they enter the Fire to receive a measure of punishment according to what they disobeyed, and the disbelievers look at them saying: "What your profession of 'There is no god but Allah' has availed you nothing; you are with us in the Fire." The Truth, glory be to Him, becomes aware of this and becomes jealous for everyone who said "There is no god but Allah," and He says: "Bring them out, purify them, and return them to Paradise." Then the disbelievers will say: "Would that we had been Muslims, so that we might leave the Fire and join the people of Paradise."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 15, verse 3:

And "dharhum" (leave them) is a command to leave them alone and let them be. He, glory be to Him, said "dharhum" once, and once He said: ﴿And leave Me with the deniers, the possessors of luxury﴾ (Surah al-Muzzammil, 11), meaning: leave them to Me, for it is I who will punish them, and it is I who know the term of respite and the term of punishment. The present tense derived from "dharhum" is "yadharu," and the Almighty said: ﴿and [they] leave you and your gods﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 127). No past tense of it is used in the language, except in what is related from the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Leave the Abyssinians as long as they leave you" (dharoo al-yaman ma dharoukum), meaning: leave them as long as they leave you.

Another verb shares this meaning, namely "da'" (da'a), meaning "leave." It has been said that the Arabs did not use the past tense of "yada'" and "yadharu," except in a reading, in the saying of the Almighty: ﴿Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested [you]﴾ (Surah al-Duha, 3).

And here the Almighty says: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 3).

We too eat, and there is a difference between eating as fuel for movement and eating for pleasure and enjoyment. Animals eat to obtain energy, as evidenced by the fact that when they are full, no one can force them to eat an extra stalk of clover.

As for man, after he eats and washes his hands, then sees a new kind of food, he stretches out his hand to eat from it. That is because man eats out of desire and enjoyment, in addition to eating as fuel for movement.

The difference between us and them is that we eat so that energy is formed in us. If pleasure comes with the food, then welcome to it; for we sometimes eat and enjoy it, but food does not agree with us; rather it tires us, so we seek digestives such as carbonated waters and medicines.

For this reason we find the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "A few morsels are enough for the son of Adam to keep his back upright." That is, he (ﷺ) forbids us to eat only out of desire and pleasure.

Let us note the difference between the food of this world and the food of the Hereafter. There we will eat food that we enjoy and that agrees with us; whereas in this world we are sometimes compelled to eat food without salt and boiled so as to preserve our health and not tire us; it is wholesome but not pleasant food, whereas the food of the Hereafter is both pleasant and wholesome.

On this basis we understand the Almighty's saying: ﴿Leave them to eat and enjoy themselves﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 3), meaning: that they eat eating intended purely for the sake of pleasure.

The Almighty then continues: ﴿and let hope distract them﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 3), meaning: that they set for themselves happy goals which distract them from a means by which they might benefit. That is why the Arab proverb says: "Hope without work is theft." So long as you hope for something, you must serve it with work in order to achieve it. But the example of deceptive hope is what the Almighty related on the tongue of one whom blessing deluded, when he said: ﴿I do not think this will ever perish, and I do not think the Hour will be established﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 35–36).

But the Hour will be established in spite of the noses of false hopes and the deceptive mirage. The Almighty says:

﴿and let hope distract them; so they will soon know﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 3). The word "sawfa" (soon/will) indicates that time is somewhat delayed; verbs such as "ya'lamu" mean that a person may know now, and know shortly after now; but when we say "sawfa ya'lamu" (he will know), it encompasses all times. Victory is achieved for the believers by permission of Allah always; as for those who do not believe, they will surely wish for faith, as we have said and explained before.

Thus we see that His saying ﴿so they will soon know﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 3) encompasses all times. The Almighty has in this world done things that herald the truth of His promise. Those who think they control all of life are surprised by an earthquake that destroys everything, despite the advances in what is called "remote sensing" and other branches of applied science.

At the same time, we see donkeys, which we accuse of not understanding anything, rush out before an earthquake to open country, far from the stables that may collapse upon them; and in such instinctive behaviour among animals is a lesson and a rebuke to human conceit: however far pride leads him, and however he claims to hold the reins of knowledge, he is still ignorant and ignorant.

Likewise we find those who say of rainy lands that their water never ceases, and therefore their greenness never fails. Then those lands are struck by a drought whose cause they do not know; and in all of this is a warning to mankind lest they fall captive to conceit.

Its meaning: He, glory be to Him, does not command the destruction of any town except at the term written for it. He makes it one of the examples which those who come after it see, perhaps they will take warning and recognize the reality of faith.

Almighty Allah has said: ﴿And Allah presents an example: a town that was secure and at ease, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it denied the favours of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do.﴾ (Surah An-Nahl)

A near example within living memory is Lebanon, which lived until before the fifties as a country where you could not find a decent hotel. Then it flourished and prospered in the sixties and seventies; corruption spread through it. So the people of knowledge of Allah said: "It is bound to be struck by what strikes the towns that are ungrateful for the favours of Allah."

That indeed happened: the civil war broke out in it, and the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, applied to it: ﴿And He makes some of you taste the violence of others...﴾ (Surah Al-An'am). This is what happens in the world, and these are precursors that confirm the truth of what will happen in the Hereafter. Glory be to the One who said: ﴿And there is no town but We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with severe punishment. That is in the Book inscribed.﴾ (Surah Al-Isra')

Naturally, this is what happens to any town whose people are wrongdoers, because Allah, the Truth, does not wrong even the weight of an atom. I recall that the tafsir of al-Nasafi was confiscated in an earlier era, because its author said, when commenting on this verse: "So-and-so narrated to me from so-and-so that such-and-such will happen in such-and-such town; and another town will see such-and-such," until he came to Egypt and said explicitly: "A man from Juhayna will enter Egypt, so woe to its people, and woe to the people of Syria, woe to the people of al-Ramla, woe to the people of Palestine, and he will not enter Bayt al-Maqdis."

Since the Truth, glory be to Him, has said: ﴿That is in the Book inscribed﴾ (Surah Al-Isra'),

He makes some of His creation aware of some of His secrets, so there is no objection to our seeing some of those secrets upon their tongues. When that story spread, and they related it to the ruler who was present at the time, and they said to him: "You are from Juhayna, and they mean you," the tafsir of al-Nasafi was confiscated.

Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, has left us in this world an example that confirms His truthfulness regarding what He relates of the threat to some towns, so that we may believe what may be after the Day of Resurrection. When the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We did not destroy any town but it had a known decree﴾ (Surah Al-Hijr, 4), no one may say: "That did not happen to such-and-such town," because every matter has a term.

That is: He, glory be to Him, has appointed for every nation a term and an end. When the appointed term comes to its close, its end arrives. No created being can advance beyond its term, and no one can delay from the time of its end.

Here they are mocking the Messenger and the Qur'an. If they truly believed in the Qur'an and the Messenger, they would not have described him ﷺ as a madman. Those who said this were four of the great disbelievers: Abdullah ibn Abi Umayya, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith, Nawfal ibn Khuwaylid, and al-Walid ibn al-Mughira. It was also reported from Ibn 'Abbas that they were al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi and Habib ibn Amr al-Thaqafi. It was reported from Mujahid that they were Utba ibn Rabi'a and Kinana ibn Abd Yalil.

The apparent meaning of their statement is a clear contradiction. Whether they like it or not, they acknowledge the Qur'an as a "reminder" (dhikr). In the Arabic language, dhikr (reminder, remembrance) has several meanings, among them honour and nobility, and it has been applied to the Qur'an, as the Truthful One, glorified is He, said: ﴿And indeed, it is a reminder for you and your people, and you will be questioned.﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf: 44).

They had already tried to find faults in this Qur'an and found none. How then can they describe as a madman the one upon whom this Qur'an was revealed, when they had earlier testified to his truthfulness and trustworthiness? The Truthful One, glorified is He, willed to vindicate His Messenger ﷺ and said: ﴿And indeed, you are of a great character.﴾ (Surat al-Qalam: 4).

In accusing the Messenger ﷺ, they did not notice that they addressed him with the words "O you" (ya ayyuha), which is the same form of address that Allah uses toward him. Thus the Truthful One, glorified is He, caused this respect and honour for the Messenger ﷺ to pass across their tongues without their being aware of it. This is by His will, glorified is He, when the people of obstinacy utter the truth without realising it.

Indeed, the Truthful One, glorified is He, said of the hypocrites that they said: ﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah until they disperse.﴾ (Surat al-Munafiqun: 7). That is, do not spend on those who are with the Prophet ﷺ until they become hungry and leave his side. Yet they call him "the Messenger of Allah." Did they believe in that? Or is this the overpowering of the truth?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 15, verse 7:

We know that in the language there are words that indicate a demand and the speaker's desire that the listener bring about what follows them. Among these words are "lawla" (why not / if only) and "lawma." "Lawla" comes for wishing (tamanni) and for the desire for what follows it to occur. If what follows it is a negation, then it expresses your desire that it not occur, as in your saying, "If Zayd had come, I would have honored him," but the coming did not happen, and likewise the honoring.

The disbelievers here said what Allah, glorified is He, related of their words: ﴿Why do you not bring us the angels?﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:7).

They had previously said:

﴿Why has not an angel been sent down to him so that he might be a warner along with him?﴾ (Surah al-Furqan, 25:7). It seems they were asking for an angel to descend with the Messenger to keep him company and so that they would believe that he is a messenger from Allah. So was their belief, conditioned on this stipulation, a belief in the Messenger or a belief in the angel? The Qur'an had already addressed this matter in the words of the Truth, glorified is He:

﴿Nothing prevented the people from believing when the guidance came to them except that they said, "Has Allah sent a human as a messenger?"﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:94). It seems they made their faith in the Messenger conditional on his not being an angel but of the human kind. The reply to them came:

﴿If there were angels walking calmly on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 17:95).

So, if a messenger came down from the heaven as an angel, he would not be able to walk calmly on the earth, let alone be an example and model for mankind, because he would be of a different kind from humans.

And if an angel descended to them as they claimed and said to them, "Do this and do not do that, be upright and seek forgiveness, and glorify Him morning and evening," they would have replied to him, "You are an angel to whom the word of the Truth applies: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ (Surah al-Tahrim, 66:6)." 

"You are not fit to be an example for us. Moreover, how can you speak with an angel when he is of a different nature? Humans cannot rise to his level to take from him, and he cannot descend to the level of humanity to take from them." Therefore Allah, glorified is He, willed to send the Messenger from the kind of humans.

Thus Allah, glorified is He, refuted their argument against believing in the Messenger, because he did not come from the kind of angels; and He refuted their request that angels descend with the Messenger to support him in the truthfulness of his message from Allah.

Thus Allah, glorified is He, teaches us that He does not send down the angels except by the will of His wisdom, glorified is He. Had the angel been sent down as they requested, to assist the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in conveying the message from Allah, then the angel would either take the form of a human, in which case they would not be able to distinguish the angel from a human, or he would take the form of an angel, in which case humans could not see him, for otherwise they would perish.

This is because humans cannot bear communication with the power that Allah has placed in the angels. And Allah, the Exalted, is the One who said: ﴿Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved﴾ (Surah al-An'am).

Had Allah made him in the form of a man and they communicated with him, the matter would have been confused for them, and they would have thought that the angel was a human like themselves. And concerning this Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them as they are confusing﴾ (Surah al-An'am).

Allah, the Exalted, did not send down the angels because He did not will to destroy them while the Messenger of Allah was among them. Allah, the Exalted, has said:

﴿And Allah would not punish them while you are among them, and Allah would not punish them while they seek forgiveness﴾ (Surah al-Anfal).

Most of them believed, entered the religion of Allah afterward, and sought forgiveness for their sins, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful, because Islam erases what came before it. And when we look at the beginning of the verse, we find that He, glorified is He, said: ﴿We do not send down the angels except with truth...﴾ (Surah al-Hijr).

Had the angels descended, it would have been a punishment for them. So when Allah gives a people a sign they requested, either they believe, or He destroys them. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We withhold not from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them﴾ (Surah al-Isra). Allah, the Exalted, did not answer them with the signs and miracles they requested, because those before them denied them previously, and they wish to deny as well; even if the sign were sent down, they would deny it. And when they deny a sign proposed by themselves, then We must destroy them. As for if they deny a sign sent down from Allah, then Allah gives them respite.

So then: if We sent down the angels as they wish, We would send them down with truth, and the truth is that We destroy them if they deny. Allah, the Exalted, concludes the verse with His saying: ﴿And they would not have been reprieved﴾ (Surah al-Hijr), meaning: the term of the polytheists had not yet come for Allah to send down the angels to destroy them, as He had previously destroyed the earlier nations that requested signs; the angels descended to them as they requested, and when they did not believe and affirm, Allah destroyed them.

The Qur'an came after a number of earlier books, and each of those books carried God's method (manhaj). However, none of those books was a miracle (mu'jiza); rather, a miracle was sent down with every messenger who preceded our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ). A miracle usually belongs to the kind of thing in which the people to whom it was sent excelled.

Since the method was separated from the miracle, the Truthful, Glorified One (al-Haqq subhanahu) required those who carried those books of method to preserve them, and this was a obligation (taklif) from the Truthful, Glorified One to them. As we know, an obligation is liable to be obeyed and liable to be disobeyed, and none of the earlier peoples committed themselves to preserving the books revealed to them. And we find the Truthful, Glorified One saying:

﴿Indeed, We revealed the Torah, in which is guidance and light. By it the prophets who submitted judged for the Jews, and the rabbis and the scholars, by what they were entrusted with of the Book of God...﴾ (Surah al-Ma'ida, 44)

That is: the Truthful, Glorified One obligated them and required them to preserve their books that carry His method; this obligation is liable to be obeyed and liable to be disobeyed. They disobeyed the command of the Truthful, Glorified One and His obligation to preserve; they distorted, altered and deleted much from those books.

The Truthful, Glorified One said about them:

﴿And indeed a party of them conceal the truth while they know it﴾ (Surah al-Baqara, 146)

Moreover, they added words of their own and said: "This is from God." Therefore the Truthful, Glorified One said about them:

﴿So woe to those who write the Book with their own hands and then say, "This is from God," to exchange it for a small price. So woe to them for what their hands have written, and woe to them for what they earn﴾ (Surah al-Baqara, 79)

Thus they committed the sins of lying and dishonesty, and did not preserve the books carrying God's method as God had sent them down to His prophets and messengers before the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

For this reason the Truthful, Glorified One did not wish to leave the task of preserving the Qur'an as an obligation placed on mankind, because an obligation is liable to be obeyed and liable to be disobeyed. Moreover, the Qur'an is distinguished from earlier books in that it carries the method and is at the same time the miracle that proves the truthfulness of the Messenger of God's (ﷺ) message.

For this reason the Truthful, Glorified One said:

﴿Indeed, We have sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 9)

When "the Reminder" (al-dhikr) is used without qualification, the meaning turns to the Qur'an, the Book that carries the method; and God, glorified is He, willed to preserve it, because it is the enduring miracle proving the truthfulness of His Messenger (ﷺ).

The Companions used to write down the Qur'an immediately when it was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). In our age we find people who do not believe in the Qur'an, yet they ingeniously devise means of preserving it. For example, someone printed the mushaf on a single page, and he employed for this the talents of people who do not believe in the Qur'an.

Something similar happened when the mushaf was recorded by modern recording means. In Germany, for example, there is a library where everything related to each verse of the Qur'an is kept in a specific, defined place. And in our Muslim lands we find those who devote themselves to memorizing the Qur'an from childhood, finishing its memorization at seven years of age; yet if you ask such a person the meaning of a word he is reciting, he may not know its meaning.

Among the secrets of the Qur'an's greatness is that some of those who memorize it possess no culture at all. If one of them stops at a word, he cannot complete it with a word of similar meaning until another person who has memorized the Qur'an prompts him.

To know the precision of the Truthful, Glorified One's preservation of His noble Book, we find that some have tried to introduce into the Qur'an what is not in it, and have tried to distort it through an approach they consider close to the heart of every Muslim: the veneration of the Messenger (ﷺ). They came to the words of the Truthful, Glorified One:

﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God; and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves...﴾ (Surah al-Fath, 29)

They inserted into this verse a word that is not in it, and printed a mushaf in which they altered that verse by writing it as: "Muhammad, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and those with him are forceful against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves." They intended by this to steal the emotions of the Muslims. But when the scholars laid hands on this mushaf, they ordered it destroyed and said: "It contains an extra word." The one who printed the mushaf replied: "But it is an addition you love and venerate." The scholars replied: "The Qur'an is tawqifi (transmitted by divine ordinance); we recite it and print it as it was revealed."

A commotion arose, and the scholars settled it by stating that any addition, even one made out of veneration for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and love for him, is not permissible in the Qur'an, because we are obligated to preserve the Qur'an as Jibril taught it to Muhammad (ﷺ).

And here the Truthful One (al-Haqq, subhanahu) consoles His noble Messenger and makes clear to him that what he has experienced of denial is nothing new; rather, the like of it happened to the other messengers before him, whether through denial, disregard, or mockery.

Since you are the master of the messengers and the seal of the prophets, your hardship must be in proportion to your mission, and your toil must be in proportion to the magnitude of the final message. And ﴿شيع﴾ (shiya', "2 sects") in ﴿Surah al-Hijr, 10﴾ means a group that has gathered around a single doctrine, whether that doctrine be misguidance or truth. An example of those who gathered around falsehood is the saying of the Truthful One:

﴿Or confuse you into sects...﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 65). And an example of those who gathered around the truth is His saying, glorified is He:
﴿And indeed, among those of his sect was Abraham﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 83). Thus the word (shiya') means a group that has gathered upon truth or falsehood. And the saying of the Truthful One:

﴿And We certainly sent [messengers] before you among the sects of the former peoples﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 10)

means: you will not be less than the messengers who came before you; rather, your journey in the message may be arduous in a manner fitting your mission, and fitting your leadership of the messengers and your sealing of the prophets.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 11:

We find the word ﴿yastahzi'un﴾ ("they mock") (Surah al-Hijr, 15:11). And we find that the Truth, glorified is He, has clarified this mockery when they said: ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down, indeed you are mad﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:6). It is as if the Truth, glorified is He, is clarifying to him that mockery may increase, and that this is evidence that you have reached among them the level of plotting. Had your plotting been small, they would have lessened their plotting. But you came with a matter that was harsh upon them, you demolished their doctrines, and you demolished even their leadership, and likewise their power, and they found nothing but mockery with which to counter you.

The meaning of this is that they were unable to resist your method, so they try through mockery to bring about weakness in you, so that you might weaken, relying in this upon the fact that every person loves to be noble among his people and honored and respected.

Here the Truth, glorified is He, wants His Messenger to prepare himself for the fact that he will be mocked, will be fought against, and will be harmed, because the mission is difficult and arduous. And whenever their opposition and harm to you intensify, know that this is among the justifications for the necessity of your mission.

Therefore we find the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, before his mission was confirmed, was taken by his wife Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, may Allah be pleased with her, to Waraqah ibn Nawfal. Waraqah recognized that he would be harmed, and Waraqah said to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him: "Would that I were alive when your people drive you out." The Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, asked: "Will they drive me out?" Waraqah said: "Yes. No man has come with the like of what you have come with except that he was opposed. And if your day reaches me, I will support you with decisive support."

Thus Allah, glorified is He, willed that the descent of the message be accompanied by fortifying him against what would befall him, so that he would have the immunity that confronts events. For as long as he would become a Messenger, he should know that the path is surrounded by harm, and thereby he would not be taken by surprise by the presence of those who harm him.

We know that immunity exists in one who, by it, prepares to face life in a place where there is an epidemic that requires an antidote serum against this epidemic, in order to protect himself from it. This is what happens in material matters, and likewise the case in matters of the spirit.

For this reason, glorified is He, clarifies this matter to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, so that his confidence in the Truth with which his Lord sent him may increase, and so that he may be firmer in preserving the implementation of His method.

And mockery, as we know, is a kind of passive warfare. They were unable to confront what the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, brought with seriousness, nor to repel his elevated method. Therefore they resorted to ridiculing the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and their ridicule did not benefit them in harming the Messenger or harming Islam. On this meaning, the Truth, glorified is He, tells us about the fate of those who mock the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him:

"Salaka al-shay'" (سلك الشيء) means: he caused it to enter, just as we thread a string into the eye of a needle. Allah, the Exalted, says:

﴿What led you into Saqar?﴾ [74:42] They will say: ﴿We were not among those who used to pray.﴾ [74:43] That is: what caused you to enter the Fire? Their answer comes: ﴿We were not among those who used to pray.﴾ [74:43]

Here Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Thus do We insert it into the hearts of the criminals.﴾ [15:12] That is: just as We inserted disbelief, denial and mockery into the hearts of the sects of the earlier peoples, so too do We insert it into the hearts of the criminals.

That is, the polytheists of Makkah, because they placed themselves within the circle of polytheism which called them to this act, and so they received the recompense for what they did, like the peoples before them who were similar to them. And sometimes such hearts find an affirmation which they deny with their tongues, just as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And they denied them while their souls were convinced of them.﴾ [27:14]

They were a people of eloquence, language and expression, and the Qur'an affected them with its sweetness and its beauty. But it was obstinacy. And here is one of them saying: "Indeed it has sweetness, and indeed it has beauty; its upper part is fruitful, and its lower part is abundant." He said this while being a disbeliever in the Messenger and the message.

We know that those who listened to the Qur'an are of two kinds, and Allah, the Exalted, is the one who speaks of one of them:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until when they leave your presence they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?" Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, and they follow their desires.﴾ [47:16] That is: his speech does not please them, and what he recites to them does not deserve to be listened to. So Allah, the Exalted, responded to them: ﴿Say, it is for those who believe a guidance and a healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them.﴾ [41:44]

This is a matter, as I always say, that relates to the receptive party who encounters the event: either he purifies his heart to receive the Qur'an, or his heart, God forbid, is filled with disbelief, and so he receives nothing from the Book of Truth. It has happened that Allah, the Exalted, placed His heavenly books into the hearts of the peoples before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), but because of the corruption of their consciences and the darkness of their minds, they mocked those books and did not believe in them.

Thus the Almighty makes clear that the hearts of the disbelievers do not soften to faith, nor do they receive the Qur'an well. That is because their hearts are filled with disbelief, just as happened to the earlier peoples, and so it is the sunnah (way/custom) of those who preceded them into disbelief. The sunnah is the manner in which the outcomes follow from their premises, and these are, in the first and last analysis, one and the same matters. And again we find the Almighty saying: ﴿The way of Allah concerning those who passed away before, and you will never find in the way of Allah any change.﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab, 33:62]

We know that the idafah (annexation construction) varies according to what the expression requires. So (sunnat al-awwalin), "the sunnah of the former peoples," refers to the cosmic matters that Allah has decreed for His servants. And (sunnat Allah), "the sunnah of Allah," refers to a sunnah attributed to Allah, and among the sunan of the Almighty is that He destroys those who deny the messengers if they ask for a sign and it comes to them, and then they persist in disbelief.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 14:

They had asked that an angel be sent down to them from the heavens. Therefore, we find that Allah, glorified is He, here brings them a proof stronger than what they requested. That is because the descent of an angel from the heavens is far easier than [the case of] a ladder being lowered from the heavens for them to ascend upon. In this there is an escalation of proof; yet they also escalate in disbelief, and they said: "If that happens, then it will surely be the work of magic."

Had Muhammad (ﷺ) been a magician, he would have bewitched them and made them all believers. Although such a matter should have been self-evident to them, they persist in disbelief, and they say: even if it were lowered to them as a ladder from the heavens and they ascended upon it, that would be by the work of magic, and the Messenger of Allah would be the one who had bewitched them, blinding their sight and causing them to imagine it.

It is as if the meaning of this noble statement is: "If We escalated to their demand and lowered for them a ladder by which they might ascend on high, so that they would say: 'Truly, it is the Real (al-Haqq) who sent Muhammad with the message,' instead of an angel descending to them according to their demand, they would not have believed; rather, they would have said: 'This is the work of magic performed by Muhammad against them.' Thus they escalate in obstinacy and denial.

We must note that Allah, glorified is He, has here used the word ﴿فظلوا﴾ [so they continued], and did not say "wa kanu" [and they were]. This is because "kāna" is used for unrestricted time, "ẓalla" [to remain/continue] for doing something during the day, and "amsā" [to be in the evening] for doing something at night. That is, each word has a set time. The intended meaning of "ẓalla" here is that Allah, glorified is He, will not lower for them the ladder upon which they ascend except at midday, but they insisted upon disbelief.

Therefore He, glorified is He, said:

﴿فظلوا فيه يعرجون﴾ [So they would continue ascending therein] (Surah al-Hijr 15:14). That is: We will not seize them at night, lest they say that the world was dark and they saw nothing; rather it will be in broad daylight. That is, even if Allah were to open a gate in the heavens through which they ascend to the exalted assembly in broad daylight, they would still call it a lie.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 15, verse 15:

They had asked that an angel be sent down to them from the heaven. Therefore, here the Truth, glory be to Him, brings them a proof stronger than what they asked for, for the descent of an angel from the heaven is much easier than His sending down from the heaven a ladder (sullam) upon which they might ascend. In this there is an ascent in the proof; yet they also ascend in disbelief, and they said: "If that happens, it will surely be the work of magic."

And if Muhammad (ﷺ) were a magician, he would have bewitched them and made them all believers. Although such a matter should have been self-evident to them, they persist in disbelief and say: if He had sent down a ladder from the heaven and they had ascended upon it, that would have been by the act of magic; and the Messenger of God would have been the one who bewitched them, blinding their eyes and causing them to imagine it.

It is as if the meaning of this noble saying is: if we went to the furthest point of their demand, and sent down for them a ladder by which they could climb upward, so that they would say: "The Truth is the one who sent Muhammad with the message," instead of an angel descending to them according to their demand, they would not have believed, but would rather have said: "This is the work of magic performed by Muhammad against them." Thus they ascend in obstinacy and denial.

We must also note that the Truth, glory be to Him, has come here with the word:

﴿فَظَلُّواْ﴾ [al-Hijr: 14].

He did not say "wa-kanu" (and they were), because "kana" is used for absolute time, "zalla" for working during the day, and "amsa" for working at night; that is, every word has a written time, and what is meant by "zallu" here is that the Truth, glory be to Him, would not send down for them the ladder upon which they climb except at midday, but they insisted on disbelief.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, said:

﴿فَظَلُّواْ فِيهِ يَعْرُجُونَ﴾ [al-Hijr: 14].

That is: We will not seize them at night, lest they say that the world was dark and they saw nothing; rather it will be in broad daylight. That is, even if God opened a gate in the heaven through which they ascended to the Exalted Assembly in broad daylight, they would still deny it.

After that, the Truth, glory be to Him, moves us to the cosmos to show us the wonders of His signs, saying:

﴿وَلَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا فِي ٱلسَّمَاءِ...﴾.

The word *al-buruj* (the towers, meaning great structures) refers to lofty buildings. Almighty Allah says: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be in towers built up high﴾ (Surah an-Nisa', 4:78), and He says: ﴿By the sky containing the mansions of the stars﴾ (Surah al-Buruj, 85:1).

The meaning common to all of this is a striking adornment through its lofty mass, and it may also be striking through its captivating beauty.

*Al-buruj* is the plural of *burj* (a zodiacal mansion), and these are the stations of the sun and the moon. Whenever the sun moves across the sky, it passes from one *burj* to another, and so does the moon, in confirmation of the saying of Almighty Allah: ﴿Each in an orbit is swimming﴾ (Surah al-Anbiya', 21:33).

He says: ﴿It is He who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light and determined for it phases that you may know the number of years and the account﴾ (Surah Yunus, 10:5). That is, so that we may regulate all timekeeping by the light of that movement of the sun and the moon. When we open any newspaper, we read what is called the "zodiac columns" (*abwab al-ta'li'*), which contain the names of the signs: Aries (*burj al-hamal*), Capricorn (*burj al-jadi*), Virgo (*burj al-adhra'*), and others. These are Syriac names for the stations through which the stars' signs pass. A poet says:

*The Bull carried the Crab's pod, the Scorpion, the Archer, the Goat, the Water-carrier,*
*and the Lion grazed on the Spica and the Scales,*
*and the Fish—we do not know of what mother the Syriacs are.*

There are twelve signs, and each sign has measures in the atmosphere and the weather. When we read the Qur'an, we find the saying of Almighty Allah: ﴿And landmarks; and by the stars they are guided﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 16:16). Some people try to find an influence of each sign on those born while that sign is rising. Perhaps whoever says this reaches some understanding of some of Allah's secrets in His creation. For He, glory be to Him, has sworn by the positions of the stars, and said: ﴿So I swear by the positions of the stars, and indeed it is a great oath, if you only knew﴾ (Surah al-Waqi'ah, 56:75–76).

Some say that every person has a star that is born with him and dies with him, which is why it is said, "the star of so-and-so has set." We do not affirm or deny the truth of such matters, because they have not been scientifically established, and Almighty Allah knows their secrets best, and He may let some of His creatures know them.

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, we find the saying of Almighty Allah: ﴿And We have placed in the sky great stars [mansions]...﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:16). That is, there is an affirmation of the existence of those mansions in the sky. This placement is not for their influence on the atmosphere, nor because they are signs by which we are guided, nor even for their effect on heat, humidity, and plants. Rather, above all that, they perform a great aesthetic function, namely, to be an adornment for everyone who looks at them. Therefore Almighty Allah said: ﴿and We have adorned it for the observers﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:16). Something may be useful yet have no aesthetic value, whereas Almighty Allah willed to give the stars an aesthetic value. He created man, and He knows that the self has many faculties, and each faculty has its nourishment.

The nourishment of the eye is a beautiful view; the ear's nourishment is a beautiful sound; the nose's nourishment is a pleasant scent; the tongue is pleased by a pleasant taste; and the hand is pleased by a smooth texture. This is what we know of the nourishment of the faculties of the five senses that we are aware of.

There are other faculties in the human soul, each of which needs a specific nourishment. Giving one faculty of the soul more than the nourishment required for it may cause that faculty to become corrupted; likewise, depriving a faculty may cause an innate corruption in the human soul.

The balanced person is one who nourishes his faculties in a balanced way. Psychological illness sometimes appears as a result of the lack of nourishment for one of the psychological faculties, and treating this illness requires a journey of searching for the hungry faculty within the human soul.

Thus we find in the human soul a faculty for seeing adornment, and how adornment attracts the human soul! The clear example of this is the existence of interior designers who arrange lighting in homes in various artistic forms. Therefore Almighty Allah says of the mansions of the stars: ﴿and We have adorned it for the observers﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:16).

And we find Him, glory be to Him, saying about some of the blessings He has bestowed upon us: ﴿And horses, mules, and donkeys [He created] for you to ride and as adornment...﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 16:8). Thus Almighty Allah bestows upon us the favor of the beauty of what He created and subjected for us. The matter does not stop there; rather, these animals serve man in other matters: ﴿and they carry your loads to a land you could not reach except with difficulty to yourselves. Indeed, your Lord is Kind and Merciful﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 16:7). He, glory be to Him and exalted, is the One who gave those beasts a beautiful appearance, for He says: ﴿And for you in them is beauty when you bring them home at evening and when you send them out to pasture﴾ (Surah an-Nahl, 16:6).

He, glory be to Him, did not create blessings merely for us to use them for their available purposes; rather, some of them stir the feelings of beauty that He placed within us. Whenever we are moved by beauty, we find the beautiful, and in His oneness is the singling-out of His majesty.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 17:

We know that the devils used to eavesdrop on some of the method of Allah that was revealed to the earlier messengers before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ); and they would try to add to it from their own (sources) what would corrupt its meaning. As soon as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came, all of this was prevented by the command of the Truth, glorified is He, and He, exalted is He, says:

﴿And indeed, the devils inspire their allies to dispute with you.﴾ (Surah al-An'am)

Therefore we find the devils saying what the Truth, glorified is He, has related on their tongues in His Mighty Book: ﴿And we have touched the heaven, and found it filled with strong guards and burning flames. And we used to sit in it on listening posts; but whoever listens now finds a burning flame lying in wait for him. And we do not know whether evil is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them guidance.﴾ (Surah al-Jinn)

Thus we have learned that they used to eavesdrop, taking portions of the words of the method and adding to them; so one truth appears with them alongside a thousand lies. The Truth, glorified is He, willed to refute that, so He said:

﴿And We guarded it from every accursed devil.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr)

The shaytan, as we know, is the rebellious one among the jinn.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 18:

The word ﴿istaraqa﴾ (Surah Al-Hijr) defines the meaning precisely. There is one who "saraqa" (stole), and there is one who "istaraqa" (stole stealthily). The one who "saraqa" is, for example, someone who enters a house and begins packing what is in it into bags, then leaves the house at his ease to carry them wherever he wishes.

But if there is someone in the house, the thief moves covertly, out of fear that whoever is in the house will catch him and hold him. Thus the meaning of "istaraqa" is obtaining something by stealth accompanied by fear.

The disobedient jinn used to eavesdrop (yastariquna al-sam') on the revelation sent down to the messengers before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). After his noble mission, the situation changed, as Allah, exalted is He, willed to guard the heaven: whenever a devil approached it, a piercing flame (shihab thaqib) would follow him.

The shihab (meteor) is a rising fire; it is a burning ember resembling a lit piece of charcoal, from which flame emerges. This is what is called a shihab.

As for when the flame is without a tuft of smoke, it is called "al-samum" (scorching wind/fire). And if the smoke is twisted, with flame coming out of it and billowing in the air, it is called "marij", as Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿from a smokeless fire﴾ (Surah Ar-Rahman). Thus we find the heaven guarded by meteors, scorching fire, and smokeless fire.

Whenever we hear the word "earth" (al-ard), we recognize what is meant by it, because there is no "where" (ayn) with the eye. And al-madd (extension) is the natural stretching-out of whatever we walk upon, from any place on the earth.

This is the observation to which the Truth, glorified is He, draws our attention. For if the earth were square, or rectangular, or triangular, we would find for it an end and an edge. But as we travel across the earth we find it extending, and therefore it must necessarily be spherical (mudawwara).

In experimental science, they demonstrate that the earth is spherical by the fact that if a person walks in a straight line, he will return to the point from which he started, since the curvature of the earth is made with extreme precision, such that the eye may not perceive the amount of its curvature, and it appears straight.

And when the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We cast therein firm mountains﴾ (Surah al-Hijr 15:19).

That is, things that stabilize it. One may ask: since the earth was created in a state of stability, did it need stabilizers?

We say: it must be that the Truth, glorified is He, created it in motion and subject to being disturbed, so He created for it weights (al-muthaqqalat, the stabilizing masses). Thus we have taken from this verse two realities: the sphericity (al-takwir) and the rotation (al-dawaran).

There is another verse in which the Truth, glorified is He, says:

﴿And you see the mountains, you think them fixed, while they pass away as the passing of clouds﴾ (Surah al-Naml 27:88).

From this noble statement we understand that the movement of the mountains is not inherent in them but follows the movement of the earth, just as the cloud moves following the movement of the winds.

He, glorified is He, willed to make the mountains as stabilizing anchors (rawasi) for the earth, so that it would not sway with us, so that it would not lean to the right or to the left during its motion. And the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We caused to grow therein of every thing in balance﴾ (Surah al-Hijr 15:19). And He, glorified is He, caused to grow from the earth every thing in precise measure suited to the atmosphere and environment, comprising the elements necessary for the continuation of life.

In this statement, He (glory be to Him) bestows favour upon us by making for us in the earth means of livelihood. And He did not stop at that; rather, He placed in it the provision of what we feed on, from the creatures that serve us, such as plants and animals, and fuel, and what He inspires us with to develop our lives through methods of agriculture and industry. Above all that, He gave us offspring that delight the eye, and all of this is subject to His will and disposal.

And His saying, the Truth: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries...﴾ [Surah al-Hijr 15:21]. That is, there is no kind of thing that does not have treasuries with Allah, the Exalted. So the thing you consider trivial has treasuries, and likewise the precious thing. He, the Exalted, sends down everything in measured quantity, and even scientific discoveries He sends down in measured quantity.

When we need anything stored in the secrets of the universe, we use our minds, which Allah has granted us, to discover that thing. An example is fuel. In the past we used the wood of trees and firewood. He, the Exalted, is the One who said: ﴿Have you considered the fire that you kindle? Is it you who produced its tree, or are We the producer?﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah 56:71-72]. Then human needs expanded, and they discovered coal, whose origin was a buried plant or a buried animal in the earth; then petroleum was discovered, and so on.

That is, He, the Exalted, will not create anything new in it. Rather, He, the Exalted, prepared everything in the earth and measured its sustenance before Adam, peace be upon him, descended to the earth from the garden of training, so that he might cultivate the earth and be a khalifah (vicegerent) of Allah in it, he and all his offspring until the Hour is established.

So if we complain of something, its source is laziness and failure to make good use of what Allah created for us and measured as our provision in the earth. We see unhappiness on the planet Earth despite scientific and technical progress. That is because we use what the Truth, the Exalted, has stored up to be a sphere of happiness for us in wars and mutual discord.

If what is spent on wars were directed toward developing the various societies, everyone would live in true abundance. But the poor organization and poor distribution that we humans carry out are the first cause of human misery on the earth. He, the Exalted, has made the earth entirely for the creatures (al-anam), so whoever finds constriction in one place on the earth should head to another place.

But political factors and other disputes among people make, in some places on the earth, men without work, and in other places, wealth without investment. We ignore His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And there is not a thing but that with Us are its treasuries...﴾ [Surah al-Hijr 15:21].

So every thing on earth has treasuries. The khaznah (treasury) is the place where precious things are stored, and the whole universe is created in the form that the Truth, the Exalted, has measured in the earth as sustenance for all creatures from Adam until the Hour is established.

If constriction in provision occurs, then know that a right of Allah has been neglected, either because you neglected the reclamation of the land and the revival of its dead land in proportion to the increase of the population on the earth, or because you have hoarded what you took from the earth and withheld what you have accumulated from others.

If you see a poor person wasted, know that there is a rich person who has withheld from him what Allah poured out to the rich as provision. If you see someone unable to grasp the causes of his life, know that another person has withheld his strength from him. If you see an ignorant person, know that a learned person has withheld his knowledge from him. If you see a foolish person (akhraq), know that a wise person has withheld his wisdom from him. Everything in life is stored, so that the movement of life may be sound, a soundness that leads to mutual support and solidarity, not to hostility and conflict.

We know that He, the Exalted, prepared the universe for us with everything in it before He created us. He did not impose obligation upon us before puberty, because obligation defines a person's choice regarding many things that relate to all the faculties of the soul: food, drink, clothing, shelter, and the control of desires, so that we do not follow the pursuit of satisfying instincts at the expense of values.

The Exalted willed that obligation not be imposed except after puberty, so that the faculties of the soul attain strength and capability, and he becomes able to beget a like of himself, and so that this obligation may be a proof against the human being, for whom the Truth, the Exalted, has stored up everything, whether in the earth, or as stored within the species or the genus.

Everything in the universe is measured: it is either a genus, a species, or individuals. The balance by which all those gifts exist is that the Truth, the Exalted, willed to bestow the Lord's giving upon all, so that it agrees with multiplicity, and so that the human being lives within the embrace of faith. Thus Allah's giving to us is a giving of lordship (rububiyyah) and a giving of divinity (uluhiyyah), and the truly intelligent person is the one who takes both gifts together so that his life may be upright.

And the Truth, the Exalted, is the One who said: ﴿Say: "Even if you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, you would withhold them for fear of expenditure. And mankind is ever stingy."﴾ [Surah al-Isra' 17:100].

Whoever does that apparently prefers others over himself, but the real reality is that he is greedy for the good reward that Allah has prepared for him in this world and in the Hereafter.

Therefore, the root of the religious act is also the self. That is why we find someone who says: "I love faith, because in it is goodness." The Truth, the Exalted, says: ﴿And indeed, he is intense in his love of wealth.﴾ [Surah al-Adiyat 100:8].

We know that if the Truth, the Exalted, had willed, He would have made all people rich, and would not have made one hand upper and another lower. But He, the Exalted, did not will that, so that the human being may be a son of change (ibn aghyar), and so that the balance of faith may be made just in him, and so that the pride of self may be shattered by the self, and so that the human being may learn that his arrogance against his Lord will not gain anything from Allah, and will not bring the human being anything at all.

All manifestations of strength in a human being are not from the human being himself, and are not inherent in him; rather they are bestowed upon him by Allah. Thus the Truth, the Exalted, willed to refine people so that they may treat one another well.

For this reason the Exalted made clear that with Him are the treasuries of everything, and if He willed, He would cast what is in them upon them all at once. But He did not wish that, to confirm for the human being that he is a son of change, and to draw their attention to the Giver of all blessings.

Just as the monotony of a blessing may cause a person to forget the sweetness of enjoying it, for example, you will not find a person remembering his eye except when it pains him, and thereby he remembers the blessing of sight. Indeed, the loss of a blessing may be what draws attention to the blessing, so that no one forgets that He, the Exalted, is the Bestower.

The sending (al-irsal) is the propelling of a thing from one place to another. When Allah, glorified is He, says that He sent the winds, we find that they are sent from every place to every place: they are sent from here to there, and from there to here.

Thus every place is a point from which the winds are sent, and every place is a point where they are received. That is why we find the winds moving in a continuous cycle. If they were to stop, the air would not move, and humanity would be afflicted with much harm from the earth, because the winds renew the air and clean places of the stagnation they might otherwise settle into.

We know that when the Qur'an speaks of the winds in the plural form, it speaks of something good, and the example is the words of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy﴾ (Surah al-A'raf: 57). But when it is singular and comes as the word "rih" (wind), it refers to punishment, such as His words: ﴿And as for 'Ad, they were destroyed by a violent, roaring wind﴾ (Surah al-Haqqah: 6).

Here the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We sent the winds fertilizing﴾ (Surah al-Hijr: 22).

The word lawaqih (فيها: لواقح) is the plural of laqihah (لاقحة). In the language it is used once for a she-camel that has a fetus in her womb, and once for that which fertilizes another so that a fetus forms in it. This is because Allah, glorified is He, willed that everything in the universe should multiply, and He made of every two a pair: either something reproduces, or energy is generated from it, like the negative and positive in electricity. He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Glory be to He who created all the pairs, of what the earth grows and of themselves and of what they do not know﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin: 36). Then He enumerated for us, saying: ﴿of what the earth grows and of themselves and of what they do not know﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin: 36).

There are things the human being does not perceive, such as the jummayz tree (sycamore fig). A person who has not studied botany does not know how it reproduces so as to bud and bear fruit, but the scholar knows that there is a jummayz tree that plays the role of the female and another tree that plays the role of the male.

Likewise the mulberry tree. There is a tree in which one cannot tell the female from the male, because it is monoecious, containing both female and male, and you may not know this. That is because Allah, glorified is He, made the pollen extremely light, so that the wind carries it from place to place.

We have not seen how the olive tree, the mango tree or the guava tree is pollinated, and that is so that we may take a lesson from the precision of His creation, glorified is He.

The example I always give is of the water that falls on a mountain: after a few days you find the mountain filled with green grass. This means that the mountain contained seeds of those grasses, which were waiting for the water in order to sprout.

The scholars have come to know that once maleness matures in a plant, it is exposed and waits for the wind, the suitable atmosphere and the suitable environment to carry it from place to place.

That is why we find some mountains green after the winds have blown and the rain has fallen, because the pollen grains were carried by the wind, and the rain came so that the plants would find an opportunity to grow.

You may find a mountain half green and half barren, because the winds carried pollen to the green half and did not carry the grains to the other half of the mountain. Thus we find that the Truth, glorified is He, has given the winds a cycle by which they move from place to place and circulate through all places.

He, glorified is He, continues in the same verse: ﴿and sent down water from the sky﴾ (Surah al-Hijr: 22).

It has become clear to us that water itself arises from a process of fertilization, and in it is maleness and femaleness. In this sense the Truth, glorified is He, says: ﴿and We gave it to you to drink, and you are not its keepers﴾ (Surah al-Hijr: 22). That is, you would not be able to store the water, because you are not trustworthy with it. If Allah has guided us to store water, then that is from the bounty of Allah. So let no one say: "We have built the dams." Rather, say: "Allah guided us to build them, after the rain has fallen, because if the rain had not fallen we could not have stored water."

Thus it is He, glorified is He, who stored the water when He sent it down from the sky, after He had guided us to build the dams.

When you want a cup of distilled water, you go to the pharmacist, who heats the water in a certain apparatus and turns it into vapour, then this vapour is condensed to become distilled water. All of that happens in the universe, and you are not aware of it.

In its outward sense it would have been possible for the Truth to say: "Indeed We cause to die and give life," since He, glory be to Him, addresses us while we are alive. But the Truth, glory be to Him, intended by this statement to draw our attention to the first death, which is pure non-existence (al-'adam al-mahd) from which He created us. And He, glory be to Him, is the One who says:
﴿And you were dead, and He gave you life; then He will cause you to die; then He will give you life; then to Him you will be returned﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah) [2:28].

In discussing death, we must distinguish between pure non-existence and non-existence after existence. Pure non-existence is that which was before we were created; then God brought us into being so that we would be living; then He will cause us to die after that, then He will resurrect us after that for the reckoning.

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, the discussion concerns the death that occurs after God has granted us life, and then we complete what He has decreed for us as our term. Then the Truth, glory be to Him, concludes the verse with His saying:

﴿And We are the inheritors﴾ (Surat al-Hijr) [15:23].

This statement means that there is a great inheritance, which is this universe that He, glory be to Him, created so that He might make us successors in it. We have added nothing to this universe that God created, for if you look at the quantity of water or food that is in the universe, and all the components of life, you would find nothing that increases or decreases. You drink water so that it quenches you, then it comes out as sweat and urine; and after death the body decomposes so that the water evaporates from it, and this applies to all creatures.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, deals in this verse with the matter of death and life and the return of the universe in the end to its Originator, glory be to Him, He is telling us about two matters that befall the life of every existing thing: life and death, and both apply to all creatures. Everything has a duration it lives through, and a term it fulfills.

Every thing that begins a task in life is born; and every thing that completes its task in life according to what God has decreed for it, dies; although we humans, within the limits of our perception, do not comprehend this. And He, glory be to Him, is the One who says:

﴿Everything is perishing except His Face﴾ (Surat al-Qasas) [28:88].

Therefore: everything that is called "thing" has its destiny in perishing; and this means that it was alive; and our evidence that it was alive is the saying of the Truth:
﴿That those who perish may perish upon clear evidence, and those who live may live upon clear evidence...﴾ (Surat al-Anfal) [8:42].

Thus we know that everything that has a task in life has a life suited to it; and as soon as its task ends, it perishes and dies, and the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, inherits everything after every living thing has perished, and He, glory be to Him, is the One who says:

﴿Indeed, We inherit the earth and whoever is upon it, and to Us they will be returned﴾ (Surat Maryam) [19:40].

He thus inherits the one who leaves and what is left behind, and He is the Creator of everything. The inheritance of the Truth, glory be to Him, differs from the inheritance of creatures: when a created being inherits from another, it first places him in the dust, then inherits what he left behind; but the Truth, glory be to Him, inherits both together, the created being and what he left.

Therefore we see those who are dear to a deceased person may hold on to the wooden bier that carries the body, and refuse, out of excessive love, to let it leave his house; yet if we left it to them for a week and the body swelled, they would beg those who carry corpses to take it so that it may be covered with earth, then they begin discussing what they will inherit from the departed.

Thus they inherit what is left after having committed the one who left to the dust. And if the one who left was among those who did good in faith and deeds, he enters a new life which is certainly more pleasant than his worldly life; he will eat and drink without tiring, and every desire that crosses his mind is fulfilled for him, for he is in the hospitality of the Supreme Benefactor.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 24:

"Those who go before" (al-mustaqdimun) are those who have preceded us in life and death: the people and nations who came before us. "Those who come after" (al-musta'khirun) are those who will come after us. Almighty God, by His wisdom, informs us that He has knowledge of every later one; that is, He knows us before we are brought into existence, and He knows us after we have departed. His knowledge is complete and eternal. The benefit of this knowledge is that reward and recompense follow from it. Thus, when we took life and provision, we did not escape from them far away; rather, we find that God, from eternity, knew what each of us would do.

There is another meaning, held by some, that God records the one who hastens to prayer and advances to it as soon as he hears its call, and He knows the one who lags behind in performing the prayer. This is because the effect of the words "Allahu Akbar" carries such alertness and attentiveness that it reminds us that God is greater than everything that occupies you.

We know that among the miraculous aspects of the call to prayer (adhan) is that its proclamation was made with the words "Allahu Akbar" and not "Allahu Kabir" (God is great). This is out of respect for the matters that preoccupy us in this world, which we may consider great. For this world must not be belittled, because it is the passage (ma'bar) to the recompense that comes in the Hereafter.

Therefore I always say: this world is too important to be forgotten, and at the same time it is too trivial to be an ultimate goal. You, in this world, travel across the earth and strive for your sustenance and the sustenance of those you support, and this sustenance should help you in worship.

So no one should despise this world; rather, let him thank God and ask Him to grant him success in it, and let him exert every effort for the success of his work, for good work earns the servant good recompense. And as soon as the believer hears "Allahu Akbar," he must turn toward the One who is truly greater, who is God, Glorified is He, and perform the prayer. This is the meaning drawn from "those who go before" to the prayer and "those who lag behind" from it.

Among the scholars there are those who have observed various remarks on this noble verse: its meaning may be general, encompassing all time, and it may be of a particular sense, such as the meaning of those who go before to the prayer and those who lag behind from it.

The meaning may be even more particular than that. When we pray, we stand in rows, with the men standing first, then the children, then the women. Some men advance to the front of the rows so that their eyes do not fall upon a woman, and some may resort to trickery and stand in the back rows in order to see the women. Thus God, Glorified is He, made clear that such matters are not hidden from Him, for He is the Knower of secrets and what is more hidden than them.

Or the meaning may be: those who go forward to jihad in the way of God, or those who hang back from jihad in His way. As for one who dies a natural death, that is, upon his bed, he has no part in this matter.

As for when the call to jihad is issued, and he offers himself to war, fights, and attains martyrdom, then God, Exalted is He, knows the one who advances to meet Him out of love and striving for the exaltation of the religion.

It may be that, in outward appearance and in the eyes of others who dislike life, he seems to be one who hates life; but in reality he loves life more than those who claim to love it, because he possesses the certainty of faith that the Creator of this world deserves that jihad be undertaken in the cause of the values He desired as a method by which the balance of the cosmos is kept upright; and if he is martyred, God has promised him eternity in Paradise and its bliss.

We find Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) saying to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Pray for me, O Messenger of Allah, that I may be martyred." The Noble Prophet replied to him: "Let us enjoy yourself, O Abu Bakr" (mata'na bi-nafsika ya Aba Bakr).

Accordingly, the one who lags behind here is not subject to blame, because faith needs someone to guard and establish it, just as it needs someone to affirm that faith in God is dearer than life itself; and the one who advances to fight and attains martyrdom in the way of God is the other side of that same truth.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 25:
