That is: the One who has charge of your upbringing, O Muhammad, will not leave those who disputed with you, opposed you, humiliated you and harmed you without punishment. The phrase ﴿He will gather them﴾ (Surat al-Hijr, 15:25) suffices as proof that God stands in ambush for them (yaqifu lahum bil-mirsad). They denied resurrection (al-ba'th), yet none of them dared to deny death. God, glory be to Him, had already described resurrection in His true words: ﴿Then indeed, after that, you will die. Then indeed, on the Day of Resurrection, you will be resurrected﴾ (Surat al-Mu'minun, 23:15-16).

They had been heedless of preparing for what comes after death, as though they doubted that it was coming. So He brought them the news of death as a certain matter, and preceded it with (huwa) to confirm that it will certainly occur. The gathering is attributed to God, glory be to Him, and He is able to do it, just as He was able to bring about creation from non-existence. There is therefore no basis for doubt or denial.

Then He brought them the news of resurrection, about which they harbour doubt, a matter for which God had already presented clear proofs. For this reason He stated the news accompanied by the separating pronoun (damir al-fasl): ﴿He will gather them﴾ (Surat al-Hijr, 15:25). And He, glory be to Him, manages all affairs with wisdom and power, for He is the All-Knowing of what wisdom requires, with a knowledge that encompasses every aspect and direction.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 26:

Glorified is He. Here He speaks about the creation of man after having spoken about the creation of the universe and what He prepared in it for him, so that the universe may receive the vicegerent (khalifah) of God. He makes clear that He created him from ṣalṣāl, which is dry clay.

And He, glorified is He, has brought the account of creation in this surah, which contains the account of the spreading out of the earth; the coming of the winds; the manner in which water is sent down from the sky; how He measured sustenance in the earth; how He placed firm mountains (rawāsī) in the earth; and how He made everything measured.

He, glorified is He, opened the surah with His saying: ﴿These are the verses of the Book and a clear Qur'an﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:1). That is, He opened the surah by speaking of the guardian of the values of human movement; then He spoke of the material from which life comes. Thus the discourse included both the essential foundation of values, which is the Qur'an, and the foundation of matter. This was a natural matter, and I indicated it earlier by my speaking about the designer of any of the modern devices, who first determines the purpose of the device, then sets out a schedule and program for the maintenance of each of those devices.

Thus was God's creation of man, whom He willed to be His vicegerent on earth. He gave him the foundations of matter and the foundations of values. He brought the discussion of the foundations of values first, because they will sustain human life so that it becomes a life that does not end, which is life in this world and the Hereafter.

This statement makes clear to us that Adam was not the first to settle the earth; rather, there was a creation before Adam. When the scholars of geology and paleontology tell us that there is evidence of the existence of some buried living things, proving that there was life fifty thousand centuries ago,

we say to them: your statement is correct.

When some people hear the statement of these scholars, they say: those animals must have existed in the time of Adam, peace be upon him. These people overlook the fact that God, the Truth, did not tell us that Adam was the first to inhabit the earth; rather, He willed to create us and to give us the task of vicegerency on earth.

And God, the Truth, is the one who says: ﴿If He wills, He can take you away and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for God﴾ (Surah Fatir, 35:16-17). That is, the creation of others than us is a possibility, and likewise the creation before us is a possibility.

We know that the creation of Adam has been taken in multiple fragments in the Noble Qur'an, which together amount to the story with all its events and pillars. This is not repetition in the Qur'an; rather, the Qur'an brought each fragment in the place suited to it. For it is not a history book of mankind, but a book of values and a method, and it wants to establish in people the values that protect them and guard them from any deviation, and it wants to cultivate in them awe.

The Truth, glorified is He, has treated the manner of the creation of man in many surahs of the Qur'an: al-Baqarah, al-A'raf, al-Hijr, al-Isra', al-Kahf, and Surah Sad.

He, glorified is He, said by way of example in Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed I will make on earth a vicegerent." They said, "Will You place upon it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood, while we exalt You with praise and sanctify You?" He said, "Indeed, I know that which you do not know"﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:30).

This statement from God to the angels came at the time God created Adam, before the matter of Adam's descent to earth began.

The question of the creation of man has also drawn long debate from those who wish to find fault with the Qur'an, asking: how does it say at one time that man is created from water, at another from clay, and at another from ṣalṣāl like pottery?

We say: all of that is a description of the stages of creation. He, glorified is He, knows best who has created, just as He created the heavens and the earth, and the Truth did not make any of the creatures witness how He created the creatures:

﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor was I one to take misguiding ones as supporters﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 18:51). And it is of His mercy, glorified is He, that He left in the perceptible and material aspects of life that which confirms His truthfulness in the unseen matters. So when He says at one time that He created every living thing from water, He is truthful in what He said, because water constitutes most of the human body, for example.

And when He makes clear that He created man from clay, earth when mixed with water becomes clay, and when clay remains for a time it becomes ṣalṣāl; and when He says: ﴿So when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down to him in prostration﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:29).

All of this is among the unseen matters, which He explains to us by its opposite in the material reality that we touch. When death occurs, which is the undoing of life, we find the spirit is the first thing that leaves the body; and it was the last thing to enter the body during creation.

After that, vitality begins to depart from the corpse; the corpse turns into something resembling ṣalṣāl; then the water evaporates from the corpse, to become afterwards dust.

Thus in death we witness the undoing of life, the manner in which the stages of creation begin, but in reverse: water first, then dust, then clay, then ṣalṣāl which resembles black mud altered over time (ḥama' masnūn), then the breathing of the spirit. God, the Truth, has spoken truly when He made clear to us in the material opposite what He informed us of in the unseen world.

Likewise, we find that those who make conjectures that the sun was created before the earth, and that the earth was part of the sun and then separated from it, must know that what they say is a matter they have not witnessed, and these are matters that no one can study in an experimental laboratory. The Qur'an has said about the people of this vain talk: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves, nor was I one to take misguiding ones as supporters﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 18:51). And they have helped confirm the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, which called them "misguiders," because they lead people astray from the truth into falsehood.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 15, verse 27:

We know that the word (al-samum) refers to a flame that has no smoke, and they call it "al-samum" because it sneaks (yatalassas) into the pores of the human being.

Thus we see that the element has an effect on the essential constituents of the life of creatures. The one created from clay has the properties of clay, and the one created from fire has the properties of fire. For this reason, the law governing the jinn is lighter and more intense than the law governing humankind.

The Almighty says: ﴿Indeed, he sees you, he and his tribe, from where you cannot see them.. " 27 "﴾ (Surat al-A'raf). Thus we know that the law of the creation of the jinn from the element of fire that has no flame shows us that they have capabilities that differ from the capabilities of humankind.

That is because their mission in life differs from the mission of humankind, and it does not make them superior or more excellent, for when missions are multiplied among things, comparison between creatures is precluded.

An example of this is the victory of the one who had knowledge of the Book over the ifrit of the jinn, when Solomon (peace be upon him) asked who would bring him the throne of Bilqis: ﴿He said, "O chiefs, which of you will bring me her throne before they come to me in submission?" " 38 "﴾ (Surat al-Hijr). An ifrit of the jinn said that he was capable of bringing the throne before Solomon rose from his place, but the one who had knowledge of the Book said that he was capable of bringing the throne of Bilqis before Solomon's glance returned to him. Thus the one who had knowledge of the Book overcame the power of the ifrit of the jinn.

The Almighty has related this to us in His noble Book, saying: ﴿An ifrit of the jinn said, "I will bring it to you before you rise from your place, and indeed I am powerful and trustworthy for it." " 39 " The one who had knowledge from the Book said, "I will bring it to you before your glance returns to you." And when he saw it settled beside him, he said, "This is from the bounty of my Lord..." " 40 "﴾ (Surat al-Naml).

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on surah 15, verse 28:

We have come to understand this verse in various places in our reflections (khawatir). We know that people in our time, when they wish to make a statue of something, mix earth with water so that it becomes mud; then they leave it until it ferments and becomes like clay (salsal), and after that the sculptor shapes the features of the one for whom they wish to make a statue.

Statues come in one fixed form and have no power of their own, unlike the human being created by the hand of God, who possesses, through the act of breathing into him of the spirit of God, what no being fashioned by human skill can possess. For the completeness and boundlessness of the Creator's power cannot be equated with the limited power of the creature.

There is a hadith in which the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "God, mighty and majestic, created Adam in His image, sixty cubits tall."

The scholars differed over the referent of the pronoun in this hadith: does it return to the image of Adam, or does it return to Adam?

Some scholars said: the pronoun returns to Adam, meaning that God did not create him as a child who then grew up; rather He created him in mature form. Adam looked around and found himself in that mature form, and that he had not existed an hour before; so he turned to the One who brought him into being.

As for those who said that the Truth, glorified is He, created man in His image, and that the pronoun returns to God, this is because the Truth made man His vicegerent (khalifah) on earth, gave him some of His power, some of His knowledge, some of His wisdom, and some of His dominion (qahiriyyah).

For this reason the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Take on the character traits of God."

Thus the creation of Adam falls within His being (kaynunah). The Truth says: ﴿Indeed, the likeness of Jesus with God is like the likeness of Adam. He created him from dust, then said to him, "Be," and he was." (Surah Al 'Imran, 59)﴾ And in the presence of being (kaynunah), causation (ta'lil) falls away, and nothing remains but faith in the Creator.

Tawiyah (tasweeyah) means making a thing fit for the purpose for which it is intended. God, glory be to Him, willed to fashion (sawwa) the human being in a form that permits the breathing of the spirit into him. The breathing from the spirit of God does not mean that the breathing took place by pushing life through the air into the mouth of Adam; rather, the matter is a figurative image (tamtheel) of the spirit's spreading through all parts of the body.

The scholars have differed in defining the spirit (al-ruh), and I see that it is safer not to delve into that matter, because it is the Truth, glory be to Him, who said: ﴿They ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is of the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little.﴾ (Surah al-Isra', 85).

And they all prostrated in a single movement, for they have no choice in carrying out what they are commanded. After God created Adam, His Truth, glory be to Him, honoured him by saying to the angels: ﴿Prostrate to Adam﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 116). The angels who were charged by God with overseeing and managing this new creature prostrated, namely the *mudabbirat amran* (those who arrange affairs) and the *hafazah* (guardians), and whoever has a connection with this new creature.

His Truth's saying: ﴿So fall down before him in prostration﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 29) means that the act of prostration took place directly, decisively and swiftly, and their prostration was obedience to the Supreme Commander, not obedience to Adam.

And the saying of God, glory be to Him: ﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 30) means the angels above the human level. This is because there are angels higher than them, namely the *muhayyimun* (the absorbed ones), who are devoted exclusively to glorifying God.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 31:

Thus the discussion here about Iblis came with the exception and with the punishment that descended upon him; so it is as if the matter has included him. This question has taken up a long debate among the scholars.

This debate should have been settled by two matters:

The first matter: the explicit text (nass) is the master of the rulings.

The second matter: for anything on which there is no text, we take it by analogy (qiyas) and by what is necessarily implied (iltizam). And if a text conflicts with an implication (iltizam), we interpret the implication to what the text indicates.

Now, if Iblis was punished, that is because he excepted himself from prostration out of refusal, disdain and arrogance. So does this mean that Iblis was one of the angels?

No. For there is an explicit text in which the Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis. He was of the jinn, so he defied the command of his Lord...﴾ (Surah al-Kahf, 50). Thus the Truth, glorified be He, settled the matter: Iblis is not one of the angels; rather, he is of the jinn, and the jinn are a chosen kind like humankind; they can obey, and they can disobey.

That he heard the command to prostrate means that he was in the presence of the angels; and this means that previously he had undertaken an obligation that raised him to the level of being present with the angels. For he was a chooser who could obey and was able to disobey, but the obligation he had chosen placed him among the ranks of the angels.

The books of transmitted reports say that they used to call him "the peacock of the angels", strutting in his obedience. It was he whom God had granted choice, because he had the capacity over himself and compelled himself to obey his Lord. Therefore his sitting with the angels was an honour for him, since he sat with the pure ones, but he was not an angel.

Some scholars ranked him above the angels, and others ranked him below the angels, because he is of the jinn. But the matter agreed upon is that he was not an angel, according to the text of the Qur'an. And whether he was higher or lower, he was obliged to abide by what proceeds from the Truth, glorified be He.

We find the Truth, glorified be He, when He presents this matter, saying once ( abā, "refused"), once ( istakbara, "was arrogant"), and once combining refusal and arrogance.

Refusal (ibā') means that he refuses to carry out the command without haughtiness. Arrogance (istikbār) is refusal accompanied by a manner of pride. Here the punishment was the consequence of the act of refusal and arrogance. And how he answered the command of the Truth is recounted, glorified be He, once in the words of Iblis:

﴿I would not prostrate to a human whom You created from clay, from black mud altered.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 33)

And His saying: ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and You created him from clay."﴾ (Surah Sad, 76).

"And you say, 'What is wrong with you?' regarding the strange matter whose occurrence you want to know, as if this were a question about something contrary to what Iblis chose, the one to whom Allah gave the distinctive faculty of choice, and he chose to be among those who obey.

Let us note that the speaker here is Allah, and He is the One who knows that He created Iblis with the faculty of choice; so he has the ability to obey, and he has the ability to disobey. And He, glory be to Him, here makes clear what He knew from eternity about Iblis, and He willed to bring this out so that it would be a proof against Iblis on the Day of Resurrection."

Thus Iblis revealed what he harbored of mistaken understanding about the nature of the elements; for he imagined that clay and dried clay (salsal) were lower in rank than the fire from which God created him. Iblis's refusal to prostrate was therefore a reasoned refusal; it was as if Iblis had understood that the element of createdness is what confers distinction, and he overlooked that the command is the will of the One who orders the ranks by His wisdom, not according to the whim of any of the creatures.

Then who said that fire is better than clay? We know that one thing is not said to be better than another unless their benefit is equal; fire has its own use, and clay has a different use; and each of them has a function that differs from the function of the other.

And from God's guidance concerning the virtues of creation: the one who gilds things with gold is not regarded by Him, glory be to Him, as different from the one who kneads clay to make pottery; neither of them is preferred over the other except by the perfection of his function.

Thus Iblis revealed that what made him disdain compliance with the command to prostrate was his conviction that there is one element better than another element.

Thus the command was issued to expel Iblis from the presence of Allah, in the highest assembly, and the punishment was pronounced: that he is cast out from every good. The root of the matter is that the expulsion is by stoning (al-rajm).

This occurred because of his rejection of Allah's command (subhanahu) and his arrogance, and because of his conviction that the fire from which he was created is superior to the clay from which Adam was created. He did not consider that every creature has a mission, and that every being performing its mission is equal to the others.

Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala) willed this so that every being would carry out the causes for which it was brought into existence. Adam was created by Allah to be a khalifah (vicegerent) on the earth, for He (subhanahu) directs the affairs of causation through what He has created.

For example, fire causes food to be cooked, because He (subhanahu) willed it and made it a cause for cooking food. The fact that the Truth (subhanahu) carries out many things through effects means that creatures perform the tasks which He (subhanahu) intended for them in existence.

The true believer is one who sees in the causes that exist in the universe a gift from Allah, and sees that His hand is extended to him through those causes. In this statement there is also confirmation that the jinn too die, and that they have appointed terms just as we do.

In this ruling of expulsion there is a confirmation that He, glory be to Him, will not grant him success in repentance, nor will He pardon him in the end.

But Iblis attempts to evade (the matter) ;.

Iblis, by this request, seems to have wanted to escape death. But such a scheme cannot succeed against God or in the face of God. If Iblis wanted to remain in this world until the day the creatures are raised, then this is evidence of his wish to flee from death.

At the moment Iblis hears that, he thinks he has escaped death, since there is no death after the Resurrection (al-ba'th), and he imagines that his supplication has been answered. It is as though he has escaped by his delusion, which led him to think that he would have enough time to take revenge on the children of Adam. His not prostrating to Adam is what placed him in this grave situation.

Yet if Iblis possessed even a particle of awareness, he would have known that arrogance (al-istikbar) and the delusion that the element of fire is superior to clay are the cause of the expulsion that befell him.

This is the commentary on verse 38 of Surah al-Hijr (15), and the passage explains that Iblis too will taste death. The reason is that all creatures will taste death before the Resurrection, in confirmation of the Real's saying: ﴿And the Horn is blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth swoons, except whom Allah wills﴾ (Surah az-Zumar, 39:68). Likewise is His saying: ﴿Everyone upon it is passing away﴾ (Surah ar-Rahman, 55:26; cited here as Surah al-Hijr, 15:26 in the source). Thus Iblis has not escaped death.

Someone may ask: how did Allah speak to him?

We say: Allah did not speak to him as an honour or as a mark of esteem; rather, He made his punishment more severe, just as the Exalted has angels who are able to convey whatever He wills to whomever He wills.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 15, verse 39:

The words of Satan, ﴿My Lord, ... ﴾ (Surah al-Hijr), are an acknowledgment of Lordship (rububiyyah). However, this acknowledgment is followed, after admitting that he himself brought about his expulsion and curse, by his saying: ﴿Because You have led me astray...﴾ (Surah al-Hijr). Yet Allah, glorified is He, did not lead him astray; rather, He gave him the choice by which he could believe and obey, or disobey and be punished. Glorified is He, Who empowered Iblis to choose between doing and not doing; so Iblis opposed the command of Allah and disobeyed Him.

Iblis continues: ﴿I will surely make [evil] attractive to them on earth...﴾ (Surah al-Hijr). This makes clear that every whispering of Satan is confined only to the life of luxury and to things that ruin well-being, such as one who drinks wine, or takes narcotics, or turns to everything that angers Allah through deviation.

Therefore we find that whoever lives on an income that covers his necessities is secure for himself from deviation. We also say to those who try to regulate their financial budgets: uprightness does not cost much, and it will not lead you toward deviation.

Satan's adornment will not be in lawful matters, because Allah, glorified is He, did not forbid all necessities; rather, adornment is always in what is not necessary. Hence uprightness is an economic process, sparing a person the burden of the high cost of the forms of extravagance.

Therefore we find that those who are extravagant against themselves envy those who are upright, and try to take them to the path of deviation, because every deviant person blames himself, asking: why should I be disappointed alone, and why should not someone like this upright person be disappointed along with me? His soul fills with contempt for himself.

Likewise, Iblis was foolish in his reply to Allah, but he came to his senses regarding his station and the station of his Lord: would he enter a battle with Allah, or with the children of Adam, whom He created as a khalifah (vicegerent) to populate the earth?

Iblis defined his position in the conflict, saying: ﴿Then grant me respite until the day they are resurrected﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:36).

This means that the field of his struggle is with creation, not with the Creator. Therefore he said: ﴿I will surely mislead them all﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:39). The word (ajma'in, "all") indicates encompassing every individual, and this is beyond his capacity, after he came to know his own rank and his Lord's rank,

Therefore these servants whom You have purified for Yourself, O Lord, I shall not be able to prevail over them, because You have taken them away from the path of misguidance, since they perfected their faith, and they have reached a degree of sincere devotion (al-ikhlas al-ta'abbudi) by which it becomes difficult for Satan to lead them astray.

And the people of knowledge and illumination (ahl al-ma'rifa wa'l-ishraq) say: "You reach the honour of God through obedience to God."

Had God willed that all His creatures be guided, no one could have led them astray. But it is the might of God over His creation that has opened the way for seduction, and for this reason we find Iblis acknowledging his inability to lead astray those who have sincerely devoted their worship to God.

And we find the response of the Truth, glorified is He, to Iblis clear and unambiguous, with no acceptance of what Iblis may have thought was a courtesy toward God,

Thus has the Truth, glory be to Him, made clear that His straight path is the one that leads His servants to obedience. There is therefore no favour in the matter from Iblis, who had earlier specified the positions and directions from which he would come to lead mankind astray, when the Truth, glory be to Him, said, quoting what was related on the tongue of Iblis:

﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful.﴾ [7:17]

(Surah al-A'raf). In that statement Iblis specified the directions of misguidance from which he would come, and he left out "above" and "below." Therefore we say: when the servant constantly keeps in mind the exalted might of Lordship and the humility of servanthood, then Satan never finds a way into him.

Thus the True One (al-Haqq) subhanahu issued His judgment that Iblis shall have no authority over those who have sincerely devoted their worship to Allah, and He commanded Iblis not to approach them; it is He, subhanahu, who protects them from him. Except for those who have strayed from the guidance of Allah subhanahu; these are the ones over whom Iblis is able to lead astray.

Thus we find that "al-Ghawin" (those who go astray) are the opposite of "My servants," and they are those whom Allah has chosen to be protected from falling under the authority of Satan, because they sincerely devoted themselves and purified their souls for Allah. We will find Iblis, on the Day of Resurrection, speaking before those who went astray:

﴿And Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke my promise to you. And I had no authority over you, except that I called you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in your having associated me [with Allah] before.﴾ (Surah Ibrahim, 22)

Among the blessings of Allah upon us is that the True One subhanahu informed us of all of this in this world, and Satan will surely acknowledge all of this on the Last Day. That is because he did not possess an authority by which he could overpower us in this world, but merely a suggestion and a whisper (nazgh); nor does he possess the authority of persuasion that would cause us to do what he whispers to us.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 43:

And because the destination of these people is Hellfire (jahannam), the intelligent servant should bring this recompense to mind at the moment of choosing to act, so that he does not commit the folly of the deed that Satan makes attractive to him, or that his own self insistently urges upon him. Had the one who wrongs himself kept the punishment in mind at the moment of committing the sin, he would not have proceeded with it. But the one who wrongs himself does not link the sin with its punishment, because he separates the consequences from the causes.

For this reason I always say: suppose a person has been overtaken by the fierceness of sexual desire, and people know this about him. They prepare for him whatever desires he wishes and bring him the most beautiful women, and they make ready for him a suitable place for the sin, with food and drink in it.

Then they say: all of this is yours, on the condition that you also know what awaits you. Then they light for him a vault in the house, in which there is a blazing furnace, and they say to him: after you finish with your pleasure, you will enter this blazing furnace. What will this person do?

He will surely refuse to proceed with the sin that leads them to the Blazing Fire (al-jahim).

Thus we know that whoever commits sins is in fact slow to expect the punishment, and the truly intelligent person is the one who believes the words of the Prophet (ﷺ) in which he says: "Death is your resurrection (al-qiyamah); whoever dies, his resurrection has come." And no one knows when he will die.

And as for Hell, it is the appointed place for these deviators, along with Iblis, who refused and grew arrogant, and who resolved to lead mankind astray. The forms of punishment will differ, but there will be groups bound together by a shared transgression. Those who drank wine will be together, and those who gambled (yalʿabūna al-maysir) will be together.

For each gate of Hell there is a group that enters through it, whom some act of disobedience bound together in this world, and whom some kind of allegiance gathered in this world. Friendships formed among them in this world, and they shared in companionship; therefore they share in the punishment and the retribution.

And thus the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, is fulfilled: ﴿The intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [Surah az-Zukhruf 43:67]. In Hellfire there are places in which they are lodged: one group goes to al-Laẓā; another to al-Ḥuṭama; a third to Saqar; a fourth to al-Saʿīr; and a fifth to al-Hāwiya.

Each part has a specific section assigned to it, and within each section there are levels (darakāt), because Paradise has ranks (darajāt) while the Fire has levels descending downward.

The Truth, glory be to Him, also brings in the contrast, because mentioning the contrast, as we know, gives the disbeliever regret and gives the believer the good news that he was not among the disobedient.

The Pious (al-Muttaqi) is the one who places a barrier between what he loves and what he dislikes, and strives not to let what he loves befall him with what he dislikes. Piety (taqwa) extends to its opposites. We find that the Blessed One says: ﴿Fear God, and God teaches you﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah) [2:282].

And He also says: ﴿Then fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones...﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah) [2:24].

We have said before that the Blessed One has attributes of majesty (jalal) and attributes of perfection and beauty (kamal and jamal). Through the attributes of perfection and beauty He bestows gifts, and through the attributes of majesty He bestows trials. So He is the Forgiving (Ghaffar), the Subduer (Qahhar), the Pardoner (Afuw), and the Avenger (Muntaqim).

It is incumbent upon us to place between ourselves and the attributes of majesty a shield, and to place between ourselves and the attributes of beauty a closeness. The way to this is to follow His method, so that we do not enter the Fire, which is one of the armies of God.

Here the Blessed One says: ﴿Indeed, the pious will be in gardens and springs﴾ (Surat al-Hijr) [15:45].

They are those who did not commit sins after they had believed in God and His Messenger and followed His method. Even if sin overcame some of them, and they repented from it and sought God's forgiveness, then God may forgive them, and He may change their evil deeds into good deeds.

Whoever enters Paradise will find in it springs (ʿuyun), and what is meant by them is rivers. The Blessed One says: ﴿In it are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change...﴾ (Surat Muhammad) [47:15]. Perhaps there are springs and sources there that none knows but God, the Blessed One.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, calls them to enter Paradise in the peace of security and tranquility. We know that the peace and tranquility of this world differ from the peace of Paradise: the peace of this world is clouded by the fear of losing a blessing, or that a person should lose that blessing through death. And we know that every delight in this world is passing away. As for the delight of the Hereafter, it is a lasting delight.

Thus Allah, glory be to Him, removes from their breasts whatever resentment and enmity there was. They see their worldly companions in sin, while they are filled with rancour, whereas Allah, glory be to Him, has purified them from everything He disliked in the Hereafter, and each of them lives with purified spouses. Allah gathers them together without rivalry, and none of them feels envy toward another.

Rancour (ghill), as we know, is the hatred that dwells in souls. We also know that some Muslims differ in their views on life, yet they hold faith in Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ).

For example, Ali, may Allah honour his face and be pleased with him, entered the battle of the Camel, and in the opposing camp were Talha and al-Zubayr, may Allah be pleased with them both; both of them were given the glad tidings of Paradise, and each side had a proof that seemed to prevail.

When the battle was about to begin, Ali, may Allah honour his face, came face to face with al-Zubayr. Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Remember the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when you and I were passing by him. He greeted [us], and you said: 'The son of Abu Talib will not part from his pride.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) looked at you and said to you: 'You will fight Ali while you are unjust to him.'" Al-Zubayr then turned away, gave up the fight, and withdrew from the war.

Talha ibn Ubayd Allah entered upon Ali, may Allah honour his face, and Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Allah has given me and your father a share in this verse." One of those sitting there said: "Allah is too just to bring you and Talha together in Paradise." Ali said: "Then what was revealed concerning it is the saying of the Truthful One: ﴿And We will remove whatever rancour is in their breasts...﴾ [Al-Hijr 15:47]." The word "nazaʿna" (We removed) indicates that the penetration of rancorous feelings into souls is deep, and that their removal on the Last Day is a removal from the roots. The believer looks at a fellow believer as he looks at one who has done him a kindness; and one who was his enemy in the world, he looks at as a benefactor, because through enmity and rivalry he had made him fear that a fault might come from him.

This is because the believer in the Hereafter recalls the bounties of things, and Allah, glory be to Him, makes them brothers. For many a brother of yours was not born of your mother, and Allah, glory be to Him, is the One who said in another place: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together, and you became, by His favour, brothers; and you were on the brink of a pit of Fire, and He saved you from it...﴾ [Ali 'Imran 3:103].

It may be that you have a brother whom you do not hate or resent, but you do not sit with him or converse with him at length, because brotherhood has kinds. There may be a good brotherhood full of respect, yet neither of you seeks out the other. Allah, glory be to Him, gathers you in the Hereafter upon couches facing one another. And a questioner asked: "What if the rank of one of them in Paradise is higher than the rank of the other?" We say: the absolute bounty of Allah raises the lower to the rank of the higher, and they visit one another. Thus the state of the Hereafter differs from the state of this world, for man in this world lives out what Allah, glory be to Him, described: ﴿O man, you are toiling toward your Lord with toil, and you will meet Him﴾ [Al-Inshiqaq 84:6].

But the state in the Hereafter differs,

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 48:

Your life in the Hereafter, if you have made your deeds righteous and you are among the believers, differs from your life in this world. You know that in this world you live by the means (asbab) of God that are extended to you, and you travel through the earth in search of provision, and you strive and exhaust yourself so that God may grant you what is in those means of bounty. Then you become among the successful (al-mufliḥun) whom God guides to His Paradise. The Truth, may His majesty be exalted, says:

﴿Those who believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and who are certain of the Hereafter. Those are upon guidance from their Lord, and those are the successful.﴾ (Surat al-Baqarah) [2:4-5]

The Truth, glory be to Him, chose to use the word "successful" (mufliḥ) as a description of the believer in Paradise, because the believer has tilled the world through righteous deeds, exerted his effort to establish the method of God on earth, and raised his stature. We know that the raising of one's stature indicates that the one who works has been afflicted with fatigue, and that is in the life of this world. As for Paradise, the Truth says:

﴿No fatigue will touch them therein, and they will not be removed from it.﴾ [15:48]

That is, no weariness will afflict them there, and they will not be expelled from Paradise, because they have attained eternal abiding therein. Thus He, glory be to Him, spoke of the misguided, who were companions in the world, revelling in sins; and awaiting them is the punishment of Hellfire. And He spoke of the sincere servants who will enter Paradise; they enter Paradise, and their hearts are cleansed of any disagreement that had occurred in the world.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 49:

The address here is to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). Al-inba' (announcing, informing) is the telling of a matter that carries great weight and magnitude; one does not say nabba'a (to inform) for a simple report. The Truthful, glorified is He, has already said of this momentous tidings:
﴿Concerning what are they asking one another? About the great news﴾ (Surah An-Naba', 78:1-2).

He, glorified is He, also said of this news:
﴿Say: it is a great news, from which you turn away﴾ (Surah Sad, 38:67-68).

From the noble statement we understand that it is the telling of the news of the Hereafter and what will happen in it. Here, glorified is He, brings the news of His forgiveness and mercy, which is specific to His sincere, God-fearing servants who enter Paradise and enjoy its good things, abiding therein forever. Someone may ask: does forgiveness not presuppose a sin? We say: the Truthful, glorified is He, created us and knows that the self has whisperings; the self cannot be free from some errors, sins and waswasa (whispering). The evidence is that He, glorified is He, has forbidden many actions to the Muslim, as a protection for the individual and also a protection for society, so that society may live in stability and security.

The Truthful, glorified is He, has forbidden the Muslim theft, adultery, drinking wine, and other grave sins and transgressions, and the whisperings that lead one to corruption on earth. Since He has forbidden all of that, this means that they will occur. His method, glorified is He, was revealed prohibiting them and making the one who does them a sinner, and it obliges all who believe in Him to avoid these transgressions. Here, glorified is He, makes clear that whoever among the believers is heedless, commits a disobedience, and then repents of it, should not torment himself with those lapses; for He is Compassionate and Merciful.

When we read Arabic, the language which God has honored its people by the revelation of the Qur'an in it, we find that speech is divided into either poetry (shi'r) or prose (nathr). Poetry has a metre (wazn) and a rhyme (qafiya), and it has melody and music; prose lacks these qualities, and may be either saj' (rhymed prose) or without saj'.

If you speak in prose and insert in its midst a line of poetry, the listener can perceive this difference between poetry and prose. But the Qur'an is the speech of an All-Powerful Lord; therefore you find this verse, which we are now reflecting upon, and you read it as though it were a line of poetry: it is metrical and rhymed, "nabbi'" 'ibadi anni ana al-Ghafur al-Rahim" (Tell My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful), and its metre is from the bahr (metre) al-mujtath, yet it comes in the midst of verses before and after it, so you do not sense the difference, nor do you feel that you have moved from prose to poetry or from poetry to prose; for the harmony of meanings together with the beauty of style gives us the majesty of miraculous impact, and that is among the secrets of the greatness of the Qur'an.

Thus the account is completed: forgiveness for those who believed, and punishment for those who disbelieved and were among the people of error. We note that He, glorified is He, did not dwell at length on emphasizing the punishment, for His mercy preceded His wrath, in confirmation of the saying of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "When Allah created creation, He created mercy on the day He created it as one hundred parts. He kept ninety-nine parts with Himself and sent down to His creation one part. If the disbeliever knew all the mercy that is with Allah, he would not despair of Paradise; and if the believer knew all the punishment that is with Allah, he would not feel safe from the Fire."

We note that the two preceding verses are explained by the saying of the Truth, glorified is He: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in punishment﴾ (Surah al-Ra'd, 13:6).

Therefore we see that the two verses have drawn attention to the two stations of hope (raja') and fear (khawf), and the believer must combine them, must not postpone righteous deeds and the obligations of faith, and must seek forgiveness for sins, because Allah, glorified and exalted is He, deals with people with grace toward those who sincerely intend and make good their inner disposition. For this reason the hadith says: "When Allah had decreed the creation, He wrote in His Book, which is with Him above the Throne: Indeed, My mercy precedes My wrath."

Then the Truth, glorified is He, moves us, after speaking of the attributes of majesty and beauty in forgiveness, mercy and retribution, to a concrete, tangible matter that clarifies all those attributes. He speaks of Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and gives him good tidings; then He turns to his nephew Lut and grants him deliverance, while bringing punishment upon his people.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 51:

The word (ḍayf) indicates one who inclines toward another, either for hospitality or for companionship. They call him the "munḍawī" (one who seeks refuge), because he takes refuge with another, seeking hospitality and seeking safety. One of the meanings of "munḍawī" is that he inclined toward the light. The generous among the Arabs were people of open-handedness; their generosity was not confined to those who knocked on their doors, but they announced themselves with fire so that whoever passed along the road would see it and be guided to them. We have all read what Ḥātim al-Ṭā'ī said to the slave who served him:

Kindle the fire, for the night is a night of cold,
and the wind, O boy, is a biting wind.
If you bring us a guest, then you are free.

Thus we know the origin of the word inqaḍā (to incline, to take refuge), that is: it followed the light. The word (ḍayf) is a singular noun applied to the singular, the dual and the plural, feminine or masculine. One says: "A guest (ḍayf) came to me, so I honoured him"; one says: "A guest came to me, so I honoured her"; "A guest came to me, so I honoured them (two)"; "A guest came to me, so I honoured them (all)"; "A guest came to me, so I honoured them (feminine plural)." All of this is because the word "ḍayf" functions as a verbal noun (maṣdar). However, some among the people of Arabic grammar pluralise "ḍayf" as "ḍayfān". Let us take note that when ḍayf is applied to a plural, its meaning is that a single individual came together with others; and when a group came, and then another group followed them, we say: "Another group of guests (ḍayf) came."

Here, in the verse about which we are reflecting, we know that they are not guests from the verse that follows it.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 52:

We note that the word (سلاماً) (salaman) comes here in the accusative, and its meaning is "we greet with salam," indicating a renewed greeting. But in another verse He says: ﴿When they entered upon him and said, "Peace," he said, "Peace, [you are] a people unknown."﴾ (Surah adh-Dhariyat, 25).

We know that the Qur'an presents the story through snapshots distributed among the verses; when you gather them, they draw for you the complete features of the story. Therefore, we find that the Almighty here does not mention that Abraham returned their greeting; and likewise He does not mention his offering them the roasted calf, because He mentioned that in another place in the Qur'an. So from that verse we know that Abraham, peace be upon him, returned the greeting, and this greeting came in the nominative. Why, then, did the greeting come in the accusative in the verse about which we are reflecting? That is, they said: ﴿Peace (salaman)﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 52), and a reply was necessary, which is what the second verse brought: ﴿He said, "Peace [you are] a people unknown."﴾ (Surah adh-Dhariyat, 25). The greeting that came from the angels to Abraham is a renewed greeting, whereas the greeting that came from him was in the form of a affirmed nominal sentence, indicating permanence. Thus Abraham's reply, peace be upon him, is stronger than the angels' greeting, because it makes clear that the manner of the method is that the believer returns a greeting with something better than it, not merely returning it; so his reply carried a continuous peace, while their greeting was a renewed peace. The difference between the greeting of Abraham, peace be upon him, and the greeting of the angels is that the angels' greeting is determined by the circumstance, whereas Abraham's greeting is a method for his call and the call of the messengers. Then follows the speech of Abraham, peace be upon him:

﴿He said, "Indeed, we are fearful of you."﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 52)

And in another verse it is stated that: ﴿And he felt from them a fear...﴾ (Surah Hud, 70)

And in another place in the Qur'an He says: ﴿"A people unknown."﴾ (Surah adh-Dhariyat, 25)

So why did he feel fear of them? And why did he say to them that they were "a people unknown"? And why did he say: ﴿"Indeed, we are fearful of you"﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 52)? They came to him without him recognizing them, and he offered them food, but he saw that their hands did not reach it and did not come near it, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿But when he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he became suspicious of them and felt a fear from them. They said, "Fear not. Indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lot."﴾ (Surah Hud, 70).

That is because Abraham, peace be upon him, knows that if a guest is brought food and refuses to eat, one should not expect good from him; and you await hostility.

When he knew that they had been sent to the people of Lot, and they reassured him with the good news with which God had sent them, his soul was at rest.

So the angels reassured Ibrahim (peace be upon him), calmed his fear, and removed his anxiety, for they had brought him the good news that Allah, glorified and exalted, would grant him a boy who would attain the rank of being very knowledgeable. Ibrahim (peace be upon him) received the news in a manner that carried a great deal of astonishment.

Allah, glorified and exalted, knows that He creates creation in many different ways, so that the created being understands that its creation does not have to take one specific form. Rather, the power of Allah is absolute, and a created being may come into existence in whatever manner Allah wills. What is common is that a child is born from a father and a mother, a male and a female. Or it may happen without both of them, as with Adam, peace be upon him, and then Eve (Hawwa') was created from a male and a female. In the verse we are discussing, we find Ibrahim (Abraham), peace be upon him, wondering how they can give him the good news of a boy when he has reached this degree of old age, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Even though old age has touched me?﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 54). This means that the word "ʿalā" (على) here has the meaning of "maʿa" (مع, "with"). That is, he lives with old age and sees it as difficult for old age to coexist with the ability to have children.

I always say that the word "ʿalā" (على) has wide-ranging usages in the Noble Qur'an. Sometimes it is omitted and Allah, glorified and exalted, uses another word to convey a specific meaning. Such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 71). Crucifixion happens only on the trunks of palm trees, but Allah, glorified and exalted, used "fī" (في, "in") instead of "ʿalā" (على, "on") to indicate that the crucifixion will be violent, such that the crucified person's hands and feet will be pressed into the trunks of the palm trees. Here Allah, glorified and exalted, says: ﴿Do you give me good news even though old age has touched me?﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 54). That is: Do you give me good news of a knowing boy while I am old in age? The understanding is that old age and advanced years do not allow for the ability to have children. Thus "ʿalā" comes with the meaning of "maʿa" (with). That is: how do you give me good news of a boy when I am old in age? He said this statement while believing in the power of Allah. Ibrahim is also the one whose statement Allah, glorified and exalted, related: {Praise be to Allah, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq}, as if old age were not suited to having children.

It is as if the angels were saying to him: "We are not the ones who did that; rather, we bring you good news that God willed for you. So do not be one of the despairing." The same story recurs after Ibrahim, with Zakariyya (peace be upon him) concerning his begetting Yahya, when Zakariyya called upon his Lord to grant him a boy: ﴿He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub, and make him, my Lord, well-pleasing.﴾ (Maryam, 19:6) The good news of Yahya came to him, and Zakariyya had said to his Lord: ﴿My Lord, how can I have a boy when my wife is barren and I have reached extreme old age?﴾ (Maryam, 19:8) If you wish to know the secret of the gifts of the Qur'anic style, then read the words of the Truth, glorified is He, in reply to Zakariyya: ﴿So We answered him and gave him Yahya, and We made his wife fit for him...﴾ (al-Anbiya', 21:90)

He did not say, "We set right you two." In that is an indication that the defect was in the wife. Science has since established that a man's capacity for fertility is not limited by age, but a woman's capacity to conceive is limited by a specific age. Then, if we reflect on His words ﴿and We gave him...﴾ (21:90), we find that they establish the absolute power of God, glorified is He, in what He grants and in repairing what has been corrupted. He, glorified is He, lacks nothing; He is capable of granting, and capable of arranging the causes so that what He grants is realized.

Here the angels say to Ibrahim: ﴿We give you good news of the truth...﴾ (al-Hijr, 15:55). That is, they are not responsible for the good news, but for the truth of the good news. Therefore they said to him afterwards: ﴿So do not be one of the despairing.﴾ (15:55)

Here Ibrahim (peace be upon him) declares that he did not despair of his Lord's mercy. Rather, it was wonder at the absoluteness of power that points to the all-capable Oneness, and this wonder concerned not the occurrence of the event itself but the manner in which it occurs. In the manner of occurrence there is an admiration that involves contemplation, for Ibrahim (peace be upon him) knows with certainty the absoluteness of God's power. He had already said to Him: ﴿Show me how You give life to the dead﴾ (260, Surat al-Baqarah).

Let us note that he did not ask, "Will You give life to the dead?" Rather, his question was about the manner in which God gives life to the dead. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, said to him: ﴿Have you not believed?﴾ (260, Surat al-Baqarah). Ibrahim (peace be upon him) replied: ﴿Yes, but so that my heart may be at rest﴾ (260, Surat al-Baqarah).

An experiment took place when Ibrahim was commanded to take four birds, cut them into pieces, place a portion of each on a mountain, and then call them, whereupon they would come to him running. Therefore Ibrahim was not despairing of his Lord's mercy; rather, he was inquiring about the manner in which God brings about His mercy. That conversation was not only between Ibrahim and the angels; his wife Sarah also took part in it, for the Truth, glory be to Him, said in Surat Hud: ﴿Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this my husband is an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing.﴾ (72) ﴿They said, "Are you wondering at the command of God? The mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, people of the household. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious."﴾ (73) (Surat Hud).

Thus we find that the Qur'an complements itself, each fragment comes in its proper place, and when we gather the fragments the story is completed. Here in Surat al-Hijr we find a question from Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to the angels who brought him the good news of a child, concerning the essential purpose of their coming, which caused him to feel apprehension (wajas) of them. He looked at them and sensed that they had come with a matter other than the good news of a boy, because the good news requires only one angel.

As for these, they were many for that task.

Meaning: What is the great matter for which you have come? For al-khatb (the momentous affair) is the grave event that befalls a person. It is called khatb because it occupies the minds of all people, so they converse about it. Whenever a group of people meets another group, they talk about this matter. For this reason, the desire for marriage between a man and a woman, and his proposing to her family seeking her hand, is also called khatb. The matter differs, because her family receives the one who proposes for marriage with a good reception. And it is said: "Lawful marriage has cut off the nose of jealousy."

Here Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said to the angels: ﴿What is your business, O messengers?﴾ That is: For what great matter have you come?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 58:

We know that the word "al-qawm" (the people, a group of men) is derived from qiyam (standing), and they are the people who stand up to face events. It is intended to refer to men, not women, because women do not stand up to face events. The Truthful, Glorified is the One who makes this matter clear in His saying:

﴿O you who believe, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them, nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them.﴾ (Surah al-Hujurat, 49:11)

So if the word "al-qawm" were applied to women, Allah would have described women with it as well. This is so that we know that only men are those who stand up to face events, and so that we know that a woman has her standing in caring for her family, so she only stands up for what concerns this household. Here, the angels informed Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that they had been sent to a people who are criminals, and they are the people of Lut, who burdened Lut with denial and with the sins to which they had become addicted.

This is an exception for the family of Lot from the criminals. The criminal (al-mujrim) is one who is cut off from the truth, and crime (al-jarimah) is severance from the truth in favour of the triumph of falsehood. The name of the people came to dominate the group of criminals, and so the exception was made from these criminals, who committed crimes against the method of God and the values that Lot, peace be upon him, proclaimed. Thus the mission was one and the same: deliverance for those who believed and destruction for those who turned away and withdrew from it.

We know in the language that when exceptions follow one another on a single excepted-from term, we take the first exception from the excepted-from term, the second exception we take from the first exception, and the third exception we take from the second. The example: one who owes you says, "I owe you ten pounds except four." That means he has acknowledged that you are owed six pounds. But you look at him, perhaps he remembers how much he has paid you, and he says, "I owe you everything except one dirham." In this way he has acknowledged seven dirhams as a debt, after having acknowledged six. This is because he said, "I owe you ten pounds except four," and then added, "except one dirham." Thus he has excepted from the four pounds that he said he had paid you another pound; so what he has paid of the debt is three pounds, and seven pounds remain with him.

Here the Exalted, glory be to Him, excepts the wife of Lot from those whom He had earlier excepted for deliverance, namely the family of Lot. The angels who carry out that decree did not determine the matter of destroying the wife of Lot; rather they carry out the higher decree. It is He, glory be to Him, who decreed and commanded: ﴿Indeed, she is of those who remain behind﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:60). Al-ghabir (those who remain behind) here means "one who stays"; or it is one of the words that denote opposites (asma' al-addad). She will not be saved, because those whose deliverance was decided will leave the town, and whoever remains in it will be destroyed; the wife of Lot is among those who remain in the punishment. An exception from a negation is an affirmation, and an exception from an affirmation is a negation; so the exception of the wife of Lot from those who are saved places her among those who are destroyed.

Thus did Lot, peace be upon him, speak to the angels when they arrived at him. Their appearance was extremely beautiful, and he knew that his people were afflicted with homosexual desire (al-ghulamiyya) and practiced the abominable sin of sodomy. For this reason we find that God, exalted is He, says about Lot's treatment of the angels in another place in the Qur'an: ﴿He was distressed on their account and felt helpless for them﴾ [Surah Hud 11:77].

This is because Lot knew that his people would covet these beardless youths. Therefore, as soon as they came to him, he declared to them that they were not welcome, and he did not greet them warmly. They had entered upon him in the form of young men whose features shone with exceptional beauty, which might lead his people into temptation. Moreover, they had entered upon him with no sign of travel on their features, and they were not from the region in which he lived; for this reason he disowned them.

Thus did Lot, peace be upon him, speak to the angels when they arrived at him. Their appearance was extremely beautiful, and he knew that his people were afflicted with homosexual desire (al-ghulamiyya) and practiced the abominable sin of sodomy. For this reason we find that God, exalted is He, says about Lot's treatment of the angels in another place in the Qur'an: ﴿He was distressed on their account and felt helpless for them﴾ [Surah Hud 11:77].

This is because Lot knew that his people would covet these beardless youths. Therefore, as soon as they came to him, he declared to them that they were not welcome, and he did not greet them warmly. They had entered upon him in the form of young men whose features shone with exceptional beauty, which might lead his people into temptation. Moreover, they had entered upon him with no sign of travel on their features, and they were not from the region in which he lived; for this reason he disowned them.

So they announced to Lot the reason for their coming to him: that they might bring down punishment upon the people who had oppressed him, and who had been doubting the power of Allah, the Exalted, to seize them with a mighty, all-powerful seizing. In this there is consolation for him.
I came to you with the matter of their punishment issued from the Truth, may He be glorified; so there is no room for doubt or disputing, and We are truthful in what We convey to you.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah al-Hijr, verse 65:

"Set out" (fa-asri): you and your family in a portion of the night. It is said both "sara" and "asra," and the two converge in meaning. However, "asra" appears in another place in the Qur'an and is transitive, as in the saying of the Truth (al-Haqq):

﴿So set out with your family in a part of the night.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:65)

The word "qita'" (portion) is a plural, and what is intended is that Lut should leave with his family in a part of the night, or at the end of the night. This is the method of deliverance which the angels informed Lut of, so that he, his family and the believers who followed him might follow it. They instructed him to follow the rear of his people, by their saying:

﴿And follow their rear.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:65)

That is, that he should be at the back, and in this there is an incitement for them to hasten. It was among the nature of the Arabs that when they were in a place and wished to move on from it, each of them would load a saddle-bag (rihlah) on his camel, with his family above the camel, and they would begin the journey. The leader of the people would remain behind, and his name was "mu'aqqib" (the one who comes after), in order to watch whether anyone of the people had fallen behind, stumbled, or left something of his belongings; and they called this person a "mu'aqqib." Here the angels command Lut to be the mu'aqqib for his family and the believers, to urge them to travel quickly. Then he is to carry out another command the Truth, glorified is He, gave him:

﴿And let none of you look back.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:65)

Carrying out the command not to look back requires that Lut be at the rear of the people, because looking back takes time and reduces the speed of the one who looks back. Moreover, turning toward the place of their origin on earth may stir longing for places of memory and the land of birth, and all of this may impede the movement of the whole people. Therefore the divine command came:

﴿And go forward to where you are commanded.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:65)

Or: the Truth, glorified is He, wants no one to look behind him lest he witness the punishment, or the prelude to the punishment that falls on the people, and be seized by compassion for them. We know the saying of the Truth, glorified is He, concerning the enforcement of any of the prescribed limits (hudud) which He revealed:

﴿And let not pity for them seize you in the religion of Allah.﴾ (Surah al-Nur, 24:2)

For if anyone had looked back at the punishment, or the prelude to the punishment, he might have felt longing for them or been moved to sympathy for them, despite their punishment being due to a grave sin, for they had committed a great crime. We know that the enormity of a crime fades, while the intense pain of the punishment may remain in the soul at the moment it is inflicted upon the criminal. Or: the Truth, glorified is He, wants the saved people to be hastened away before the terror, which is the prelude to the punishment of the people who disbelieved, from the dread of this coming torment, comes upon them. Thus the command to set out with the people whom the Truth, glorified is He, had decreed to save was given, and the manner is that the departure should be in a part of the night, that Lut should follow their rear, and that none of the saved should look back behind him, so that these saved ones may go forward to where the Truth, glorified is He, commands them. It was said: the direction is Syria (al-Sham).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 66:

And His saying, the Truth (al-Haqq): ﴿And We decreed...﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:65). That is: We revealed. Glory be to Him, He had earlier spoken of the deliverance of the believers from the family of Lot; then He spoke of the punishment of the disbelievers who had deviated. The matter which the Truth, glory be to Him, decreed was that these deviators should be annihilated. And "cutting off the last of them" (qat' al-dabir) is the uprooting from the roots. For this reason the Qur'an says:

﴿So the last remnant of the people who did wrong was cut off.﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 6:45). Thus we understand that cutting off the dabir means that the Truth, glory be to Him, seizes them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, so that not one of them remains. The appointed time for this is the morning. After Lot and those with him had gone out during part of the night and their deliverance was complete, the command to destroy the deviators comes in the morning. Seizing at dawn is one of the principles of warfare; it is said that most wars begin at the first thread of the sun's light. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿But when it descends upon their courtyard, evil is the morning of those who were warned.﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 37:177). Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, willed to seize them while they were at ease, not possessing any power of resistance. And the saying of the Truth, glory be to Him, here: ﴿That the last of these is cut off at morning.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:66) does not contradict His saying about them elsewhere: ﴿So the Cry seized them at sunrise.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:73). So the beginning of the Cry was at dawn, and its end was at sunrise. Thus the Truth, glory be to Him, drew the picture clearly before Lot before the execution began; for the angels had told Lot what would take place.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 15, verse 67:

When the people of the city, from the folk of Lot, learned that a delegation of handsome, beardless youths had arrived at Lot's house, they came rejoicing and glad. Their beauty had become proverbial, and each of them could be described by the words of the Truth (exalted is He) about Joseph (peace be upon him): ﴿This is not a human being; this is none other than a noble angel.﴾ [Surah Yusuf 12:31].

And His words (glory be to Him): ﴿And the people of the city came, rejoicing﴾ [Surah al-Hijr 15:67] gather together composite scenes of the open, widespread depravity among them; they took delight in its practice and rejoiced in it. They are therefore the ones of whom the Truth said: ﴿They did not forbid one another from any wrong they committed. Wretched indeed was what they used to do.﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah 5:79]. Lot knew this about them and knew what would befall them, and he wished to place a barrier between them and the act of sexual immorality with the angels. They were his guests and under his protection, and custom requires that the guest receive the honour owed by the host; any humiliation inflicted upon the guest is a humiliation inflicted upon the host.

Al-Fadhīha (scandal, disgrace) is the tearing away of the veils that a person feels shame about, for a person may do things that they are ashamed for others to know about.

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, asks us to take on His character, He has made every attribute of beauty and majesty a portion that He gives to His creation. However, there are some of His attributes that He mentions without bringing an opposite for them. For example, He said "al-Ḍārr" (the Afflicter), and its counterpart is "al-Nāfi'" (the Benefactor); He said "al-Bāsiṭ" (the Expander), and its counterpart is "al-Qābiḍ" (the Constrictor); and He said "al-Mu'izz" (the Bestower of honour), and its counterpart is "al-Mudhill" (the Humiliator). Among His names is "al-Sattār" (the Concealer), and He did not bring its counterpart, which is "al-Fāḍiḥ" (the Exposer). Why did He not bring this counterpart? Because He, glorified is He, willed to protect the universe, so that every individual may enjoy the good deeds of the wrongdoer, for if you knew his bad deeds you would spit on him. Therefore, the Truth, glorified is He, willed to conceal the wrongdoer and show only his good deeds.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 15, verse 69:

That is: place between yourselves and the punishment of the Truth for you a protection (wiqayah); and do not be a cause of my feeling disgrace and shame before my guests because of the immorality you desire. Ittiqa' (taqwa, God-consciousness) derives from wiqayah, and wiqayah is caution and keeping far from evil. Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones﴾ (Surah At-Tahrim, 66:6). That is: make between yourselves and the Fire a protection, and be cautious lest you fall into it, by keeping away from what is forbidden, for doing what is forbidden is a path to the Fire, and keeping away from it is a protection from it. And among the marvels of this taqwa is that you find the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, saying in the Noble Qur'an, and the whole Qur'an is the speech of God: ﴿And fear Allah...﴾ (Surah Al-Baqarah, 2:194), and He says: ﴿And fear the Fire...﴾ (Surah Al 'Imran, 3:131).

How can we adopt one single conduct towards the Truth, glory be to Him, and towards the Fire in which the disbelievers will be punished? The meaning is: do not do what angers God, lest you be punished in the Fire. So it is as if you have placed between yourself and the Fire a protection by abandoning sins; and if you perform what is commanded, are content with what is decreed, and keep away from what is forbidden, then you have indeed feared God.

Ie: "Did we not forbid you from hosting people, the young men distinguished by their beauty?" And because you hosted these young men, we must do with them what we desire of indecency. They used to assault every stranger with evil. Lut tried to forbid them as much as he could, but they refused to protect his guests from their outrageous aggression, and they asked him to leave them to themselves, so that they might corrupt the earth as they wish, and not to speak or object to anything we do. This is the language of the people of misguidance and corruption.

Explanation: that is, if you are determined to commit the abomination, then why do you not marry my daughters? Some have tried to say that he offered his daughters to them so that they might commit abomination with them, but God forbid that such an act should come from a messenger. Rather, he offered them that they marry the women. Moreover, Lot had two daughters, and he said:

﴿These are my daughters, [if you must act]...﴾ [15:71] (Surat al-Hijr)

That is, he spoke of a large number, for his two daughters were only suitable for marriage to two men from this great multitude of the men of that city. We know that the daughters of every people among whom a messenger is found are considered his daughters. For this reason, the Truthful, glorified is He, states what clarifies this in another verse:

﴿Do you approach males from among the worlds, and leave what your Lord has created for you of your spouses? Rather, you are a people who transgress.﴾ [26:165-166] (Surat al-Shu'ara')

That is, Lot wanted to return these deviants to the sphere of what is right and to good conduct. And he concluded his speech with:

﴿If you are going to act [at all]﴾ [15:71] (Surat al-Hijr), to suggest to them doubt that they would humiliate his guests through this reprehensible and rejected manner.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 72:

The address here is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). "ʿUmrak" (عمرك) means the lifespan determined for a human being for the upright continuation of life. Sometimes it is pronounced "wa-ʿumrak" (وعمرك) and sometimes "ʿumrak" (عمرك), but in oaths they choose the word "ʿumrak," and this resembles our everyday saying "wa-hayatak" (وحياتك, "by your life").

From this noble statement, which the Truth, glory be to Him, relates to His Messenger, the people of illumination and gnosis (ahl al-ishraq wa'l-maʿrifa) deduced that Allah, glory be to Him, has honoured our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in that when He addressed him He did not address him by his given name, "O Muhammad" or "O Ahmad," as He addressed all His messengers. Rather, He addressed the Messenger (ﷺ) only with His words: ﴿O you the Messenger...﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah 5:67), or ﴿O Prophet...﴾ (Surah al-Mumtahanah 60:12).

In this there is great honour. Here in this verse we find another honour: He, glory be to Him, swears by the life of His Messenger (ﷺ). We know that the Truth, glory be to Him, swears by whatever He wills: He swore by the sun, by the places of the stars, and by the star when it sets. He is the Creator, the All-Knowing of everything He created; no one knows the greatness of a created thing except its Creator, and He is the One who knows the purpose of every being He created. Yet He commanded us not to swear except by Him, because we revere the realities of things in their completeness. He, glory be to Him, has sworn by everything in existence, except that He never swore by any human being except Muhammad (ﷺ). So He said here:

﴿By your life (laʿamrak)﴾ (Surah al-Hijr 15:72), meaning: by your life, O Muhammad, indeed they are in their intoxication wandering blindly. The "sakrah" (سكرة) is the mental stupor that afflicts those whose perception is disordered by a corrupt belief, an aberrant habit, or the consumption of a substance that disturbs awareness.

And ﴿they wander blindly﴾ (Surah al-Hijr 15:72), that is: they are confused by their own choice. And the punishment comes;.

Earlier, He (glory be to Him) told us that He would cut off their last remnant at dawn (ﷺ might not apply here), and here He tells us that the Cry seized them while they were at sunrise. Nowadays we see some games, such as the game of "karate," in which the player lets out a cry in the face of his opponent in order to increase his terror. We also see, in the training of the military commandos, a kind of shouting whose purpose is to put fear into the heart of the fighter's enemy. Everything that requires terrifying an opponent begins with a cry that makes him lose his mental balance; for this reason the Truth (glory be to Him) said in another place:

﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a single Cry, and they became like the dry, broken stalks of the one who builds a pen for livestock.﴾ (Surah al-Qamar).

And at another time He calls it "the Overwhelming," so He says:

﴿As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the Overwhelming [Cry].﴾ (Surah al-Haqqah).

Since the uppermost part of the city was made its lowest, this is a form of organized, directed retribution; had it not been organized retribution, some of what was in that city would have overturned to the right or to the left. But God, glory be to Him, willed to bring us the picture of what happened, to show us His power to do whatever He wills, however He wills. God, glory be to Him, rained down upon them stones of sijjil, like those with which He rained down upon those who attacked the Ka'bah in the year of the birth of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). These are stones made of clay whose true nature none knows but God, glory be to Him, and clay when it hardens is called "sijjil." God, glory be to Him, is the One who said about this very event in Surat adh-Dhariyat: ﴿That We may send down upon them stones of clay﴾ [51:33]. (Surat adh-Dhariyat)

God, glory be to Him, sent those stones upon them to annihilate them, so that not one of them would remain.

Thus was the punishment that Allah, glory be to Him, sent down upon the people of Lot a clear sign for those who discern (al-mutawassimin). The mutawassim is one who perceives the realities of what is hidden through what is manifest. It is said, "I discerned (tawassamtu) in so-and-so such-and-such," meaning he took from the outward appearance the reality of the inward state.

For this reason the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Their mark is on their faces, from the trace of prostration…﴾ [48:29]

That is: the moment you see them, you see that their features make clear the faith in their depths. He, glory be to Him, also says: ﴿You would recognize them by their mark; they do not ask people persistently﴾ [2:273].

Thus we learn that the mutawassim is the possessor of firasa (discernment, insight) that uncovers the hidden contents of the depths. And the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the firasa of the believer, for he looks with the light of Allah." The Arabic memory also preserves the story of the Bedouin who lost his camel, so he went to the qayyim of the district (that is, the chief of the place) and said: "My camel is lost, and I fear someone has stolen it." While he was speaking with the qayyim, a man came and said to him: "Is your camel one-eyed (a'war)?" The owner of the camel replied: "Yes." He said: "Is your camel abtar (without a tail)?" That is, it has no tail. The owner replied: "Yes." The man asked a third question: "Is your camel ashwal?" That is, it limps slightly when it walks. The man answered: "Yes, by Allah, it is my camel."

The qayyim of the tribe wanted to know how the man had recognized all these marks of the camel, so he asked him: "How did you come to know all those signs?" The man said: "I saw it on the road, and I realized it was one-eyed, because it was eating dry grass on one side and not turning to the green grass on the other side; had it been seeing with both eyes, it would have seen the green grass. And I knew it was abtar, cut-tailed, because its dung was not scattered as that of other camels which have an uncut tail. And I knew it was ashwal, because the trace of its right leg was deeper in the ground than the trace of its left leg." Thus the Arabic memory explained the meaning of the word "al-mutawassim."
