That is, they lie on a established road that you pass by if you travel toward this place. In another verse He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And indeed you pass by them in the morning﴾ (Surah al-Saffat, 37:137).

So this city lies on a fixed road, which the forces of erosion or of change will not erase; and those forces will not erase it unless God, glory be to Him, wills that it be firmly established and firmly fixed in its formation. This is what is called "Sodom" (Sadum).

Earlier it was said: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those who discern.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:75). It seems that among the responsibilities of the believer is to examine the outcomes of things closely, to recognize things by their marks, and to possess the insight of faith (firasat al-iman) of which the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of the insight of the believer, for he sees by the light of Allah."

Thus Allah, glorified is He, concludes here the story of Lut; and the punishment that befell them is something from which the believers must take admonition, for they received the recompense of what they had done of gross indecency.

The word "al-Aykah" (the thicket) refers to dense trees with intertwining branches. We know that Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, was sent to the people of Madyan, who had wronged themselves by associating partners with Allah. Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb.﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 7:85)

And He said concerning the companions of the thicket: ﴿The companions of the thicket denied the messengers. When Shu'ayb said to them, "Will you not fear Allah?"﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara', 26:176-177)

Thus we know that Shu'ayb was sent to two neighboring communities.

It is said that what separated Madyan from the People of the Thicket (Ashab al-Aykah) was this dense, intertwined grove of trees close to the sea. Therefore we find here the evidence that Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) was sent to two nations, in His words, the Truth: ﴿And indeed, they both...﴾ [Al-Hijr 15:79].

And Allah took vengeance upon the two wrongdoing nations: Madyan and the People of the Thicket. The Truth, glorified be He, says: ﴿And indeed, they are on a clear highway﴾ [Al-Hijr 15:79]. The imam (imam, a leader or model) is that which is followed in opinion and legal ruling, or in movements and stillnesses; or: in the path that leads to the goals. It is called "imam" because it indicates the places or goals we want to reach, since it knows every detail of this path. It appears that the People of the Thicket persisted in wrongdoing and disbelief. If He, glorified be He, seized the people of Madyan with the Cry and the Quake, then He seized the People of the Thicket by sending the heat upon them for seven days, from which no shade could shelter them; then He sent a cloud, and they wished it would rain, and it rained fire, which consumed them, as the books of narrations report. This is the punishment of which the Truth, glorified be He, said: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them; indeed, it was the punishment of a tremendous day﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara 26:189].

Thus those lessons serve as the imam that leads to insight into the consequences of wrongdoing and shirk.

The People of al-Hijr are the people of Salih, and the region in which they dwelt was entirely of stone. Their settlement is still known today in the distance between Khaybar and Tabuk. Concerning them, the Truthful One (glorified be He) said: ﴿Do you build on every high place a monument, in vain? And do you take fortresses, perhaps you will abide forever?﴾ (Surah ash-Shu'ara', 128-129).

They denied their Prophet Salih, and their denial of him involved the denial of all the Messengers. This is because the Messengers converge on the Oneness of God and agree on the general and comprehensive rulings, and the Prophets differ only in the particular matters suited to each environment in which they live. So, for an environment that worshipped idols, their Prophet affirms to them that idols do not deserve to be worshipped. Another environment cheated in measure and weight, so their Messenger comes with what forbids them from that. A third environment committed abominations, so their Prophet warns them against those abominations. Thus the Messengers differed in the particular matters suited to each environment; yet they did not differ in the overall method concerning Tawhid (Oneness of God) and the method. God the Truthful One stated about the people of Salih that they denied the Messengers, meaning that they denied Salih in what he brought of the call to Tawhid, which all the Messengers brought.

Here the Almighty briefly summarizes the signs that He sent with their prophet Salih, which call them to the Tawhid (oneness) of Allah. The truthfulness of Salih's message, peace be upon him, was embodied in the she-camel, about which Salih warned them not to harm her, lest the painful punishment seize them. But they denied him and turned away from him, and they did not heed the signs that Allah created in the universe: the night and the day, the sun and the moon, and the difference of tongues and colors among mankind.

We know that the signs (ayat) always come in the sense of miracles that indicate the truthfulness of the Messenger, or the signs of the universe, or the signs of the method conveyed from Allah. The sign of a Messenger from these is of the kind in which the people to whom he was sent excelled, yet they are unable to produce its like. This sign usually stirs the characteristic of challenge (tahaddi) that exists in man, yet none of the people of any Messenger has succeeded in producing a sign like the sign of the Messenger sent to them. The Almighty says about the people of Salih: ﴿And We gave them Our signs, but they were turning away from them﴾ [Surah al-Hijr, 81]. That is, they became arrogant and turned away from the method that Salih brought them. Al-i'rad (turning away) is that you present to a thing your side by distancing yourself from it and not approaching it; if you had approached it, you would have found good in it for yourself. When you approach the signs of Allah, you will find that they call you to reflection, so you believe that they have a Creator, and you adhere to the teachings of the method that the Messenger brought. And when you reflect on the wisdom of obedience, you will find that it relieves you of the anxiety of relying on anyone other than your Creator. But if you take matters superficially, you will not arrive at faith.

For this reason, we find Him, glorified is He, saying in another place in the Noble Qur'an: 

﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ [Surah Yusuf, 105].

In this is an obligation upon the believer, every believer, to contemplate the signs of the universe, perhaps he may derive from them what benefits others. If you look at all the inventions in the universe, you will find them to be the result of approaching them by a scholar who wanted to discover in them what would ease others. An example is the discovery of the power of steam, with which began an age of energy, and the invention of machinery that works by that energy, by which the train and the ship were moved; just as another man preceded them and invented the wheel to make it easy for people to carry loads. If this is the case regarding matters of the cosmos, then you too, if you reflect on the verses of legal rulings concerning "do" and "do not", will find them benefiting you in your life and your future. An example of that is zakat: you give a small portion of the return of your work to others who are not able to work, and you will find that others give to you if you come to need, because you are among the "ghayr" (others).

Here he reminds them of the favour by which He granted them civilization and bestowed upon them the skill of building and advancement in architecture. They began to build their houses of stone, from the stones that were found in the valley in which they dwelt, and they cut those stones in a manner that enabled them to build houses and palaces secure against the changes of weather and other things. We know that one who lives in a tent suffers from a lack of security; whereas one who builds his house of mud brick is more secure than those in tents, though less secure than one who builds his house of reinforced concrete. Thus the security of the human soul in its dwelling and its stability is in proportion to the strength of the thing that surrounds it. And if the people of Salih built their houses of stone, they were surely more secure than others. We find their prophet Salih, and he said to them what Allah, glorified is He, related in His Noble Book: ﴿And remember when He made you successors after 'Ad and settled you in the land, taking for yourselves palaces in its plains and carving out the mountains as homes. So remember the bounties of Allah and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption﴾ (Surah al-A'raf) [7:74].

But they transgressed and oppressed, and denied what Salih, peace be upon him, had brought. So Allah, glorified is He, sent upon them a blast that seized them.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 83:

They, since they had taken the mountainous terrain as a secure refuge for themselves, the Cry came from Allah, glorified is He, to level what they had built upon their heads. Allah, glorified is He, had already said about them in Surah Hud: ﴿And those who did wrong were seized by the Cry, so they became motionless corpses in their homes﴾ (Surah Hud, 67).

And He, glorified is He, also said about them: ﴿So the Quake seized them, and they became motionless corpses in their home﴾ (Surah al-A'raf, 78).

The Rajfah (ar-rajfah, the quake) is the earthquake, and the Sayhah (as-sayhah, the cry) is one of the consequences of the earthquake, for an earthquake produces a wave-like disturbance in the air which gives rise to strong sounds that overwhelm whoever hears them. According to the word of Allah, glorified is He, they enjoyed themselves for three days before the Cry seized them, as the promise of their prophet Salih, peace be upon him, to them: ﴿He said, "Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied"﴾ (Surah Hud, 65).

Thus the fortresses did not benefit them in protecting them from the decree of Allah. We know that the decree of Allah, or His punishment, cannot be prevented by any preventer, whatever it may be; for He says: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be in towers built up high﴾ [Surah An-Nisa: 78].

Thus a person cannot protect himself from what Allah has decreed for him, or from what the Truth wills to send down upon a person as punishment. And He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Say, "If you had been in your houses, those decreed to be killed would have come out to their beds"﴾ [Surah Ali 'Imran: 154].

Thus they all fell headlong into the depths of destruction, and their fortresses did not protect them from the punishment that He, glorified is He, had decreed.

Truth (al-Haqq) is that which is firm and established, which is not subject to changing accidents (al-aghyar). The "mithl" (here: the measure, the pattern) is the system of the galaxies and the movement of the sun and the moon; you find them precisely regulated, because man has no intervention in them, and the one who is subject to accidents has no choice in them. For this reason we find that corruption does not arise in the universe from the higher laws (al-nawamis al-ulya), but from matters in which man intervenes. This does not mean that man should stop moving on the earth; rather, he must observe God's method, refrain from what He has forbidden, and obey what He has commanded. If you were to apply the commands of the Truth, glorified is He, in "do" and "do not do," the affairs of the world would be set right in those matters in which you have a role, just as the affairs in which you have no role are regulated.

If you wish, read His words, the Truth:
﴿The Most Merciful. Taught the Qur'an. Created man. Taught him eloquence. The sun and the moon [move] by calculation. And the star and the tree prostrate. And the heaven He raised and set the balance. That you not transgress in the balance.﴾ (Surat al-Rahman)

So if you want your affairs to be regulated in the life of this world, then do not transgress in the balance of anything. Here the Truth, glorified is He, reminds us not to fall into the error of imagining that we will take the blessings of this world without restraint or bond, for the reckoning is certainly coming. For this reason the Truth, glorified is He, said:
﴿So whether We take you away, indeed, We will take retribution upon them. Or We show you that which We have promised them, for indeed, We are Able over them.﴾ (Surat al-Zukhruf)

That is: what God has decreed will occur without anything being able to avert it, whatever it may be, and you may see that in your lifetime, or you may see it at the moment of resurrection. The proof is what befell those who disbelieved, wronged, denied the messengers, and spread corruption in the earth. God, the Truth, glorified is He, destroyed them with His punishment, purifying the earth of their corruption; this is their recompense in this world, and there is another recompense in the Hereafter. In this statement there is consolation for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), for when God informs him of what befell the earlier nations that denied the messengers, the hardships and difficulties he suffered from his people became easier for him, and so it becomes easier for him thereafter to arm himself with patient forbearance (al-sabr al-jamil), until His promise, glorified is He, comes. "And it is not upon you, O Muhammad, to burden yourself with what you cannot bear."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 86:

He, glorified is He, has here mentioned the Name by which He created from non-existence and sustained from non-existence. The sustaining lordship (qayyumiyyat al-rububiyyah) is what supplies all the cosmos with its provision and nurtures it. Glorified is He, who summoned man into the cosmos, and who nurtures it, and the word:

﴿Your Lord﴾ (86) (Surah Al-Hijr) suggests that if some harm befalls you because of your call, and because of the ingratitude of your people before you and their hostility toward you, then your Lord, O Muhammad, will not abandon them. The Lord (al-Rabb), as we know, is the one who undertakes the upbringing (tarbiyah) of a thing until it reaches what grants it the basis of perfection, and this is not limited to this world alone, but applies to both this world and the Hereafter.

And His saying:

﴿the Creator (al-Khallaq)﴾ (86) (Surah Al-Hijr) is an intensification (mubalaghah) of creation, and it is the extension of the attribute of creation to everything that can be created, because He, glorified is He, is the one who prepared every material from which any creation comes into being, and prepared the intellect that plans any creation, and prepared the energy that acts, and prepared the interaction between energy, matter, and the intellect that designs this. What the created human does is the combining (tawlif) of the materials that God has created. And if a creator (khallaq) from among mankind exists, it is He, alone, glorified is He, who bestows upon a person ideas for him to bring to light, and then there comes one who is more intelligent than him to develop them. For this reason the Truthful One, glorified is He, said:

﴿And above every possessor of knowledge is one who is all-knowing﴾ (76) (Surah Yusuf).

Thus we have seen all human inventions develop. An example of this is the weaving machine, which now works automatically after it used to be that a woman would sit at it and toil to operate it; likewise the clothes washer, the dish washer, cars, and airplanes. We notice that everything God has created can be benefited from in its waste, such as animal dung, which is used as fertilizer, whereas the exhaust of cars, for example, pollutes the air. And the television screen emits radiation that harms the eye, and research has been conducted into that to avoid the side effects of such devices by which a person makes his life easier. As for what God creates, there are no side effects for it; for He, glorified is He, is not the possessor of acquired or granted knowledge, rather knowledge is an essential attribute of His.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, bestows favour upon His Messenger ﷺ, that it is enough for him that He has sent down to him the Qur'an, the Book that is a miracle and the method (manhaj) to which falsehood cannot approach from before it or from behind it. The Qur'an contains the perfections of the Truth, which never end; so if He, glory be to Him, has given you that, He also bears for you everything that pains you. The Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And We know that your breast is constricted by what they say﴾ [97] (Surah al-Hijr).

The Truth also says to him: ﴿We know that what they say certainly grieves you﴾ [33] (Surah al-An'am).

The Truth, glory be to Him, removed from him the worries of their accusation that he is a magician or a madman, and He said to him, glory be to Him:

﴿So it is not you they deny, but it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾ [33] (Surah al-An'am). He reveals to him, glory be to Him, that they believe you, O Muhammad, to be truthful, but they feign denying you.

The favour of the Truth, glory be to Him, upon His Messenger is manifested in that He sent down to him the Seven Oft-Repeated (al-sab' al-mathani), and the scholars agree that the word "al-mathani" means the Opening of the Book (Fatihat al-Kitab), for it is only the Opening of the Book that is repeated (yuthna) in the prayer. We find Him, glory be to Him, describing the Qur'an as "the Great"; and He, glory be to Him, judges the greatness of the Qur'an by His absolute standards, which are the standards of greatness with Him, glory be to Him. Another example of that is His description of His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿And indeed, you are of a tremendous character﴾ [4] (Surah al-Qalam). This is a judgement by the highest standards of greatness. Thus every enjoyment of this world becomes less than what the Truth, glory be to Him, has bestowed upon His Messenger ﷺ, so let no one look longingly at what He has given to others, for He, glory be to Him, has given it to His Messenger ﷺ.

We observe that the Truth, glory be to Him, has conjoined the Qur'an with the Seven Oft-Repeated, and this is 'atf 'amm 'ala khass (a general conjunction over a specific one), as the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Guard over the prayers, and the middle prayer﴾ [238] (Surah al-Baqarah). From this statement we understand that "the prayers" includes the middle prayer as well. Likewise is the saying of the Truth reported on the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents, and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and believing women﴾ [28] (Surah Nuh). Thus we see a general conjunction over a specific one, and a specific conjunction over a general one. Or we may say: the word "Qur'an" is applied to the noble Book sent down upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the first verse of the Qur'an to its last verse, and it is also applied to a single verse of the Qur'an; so the Truth's saying: ﴿Mudhammatan﴾ [64] (Surah al-Rahman)

is a verse of the Qur'an, and it is also called a Qur'an. He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed﴾ [78] (Surah al-Isra').

At dawn we do not recite the whole Qur'an, but only part of it, yet what we recite is called a Qur'an. Likewise the Truth, glory be to Him, says: ﴿And when you recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed barrier﴾ [45] (Surah al-Isra'). He does not recite the whole Qur'an, but part of it; therefore every verse of the Qur'an is a Qur'an. The Truth, glory be to Him, has given His Messenger ﷺ the Seven Oft-Repeated and the Great Qur'an, and these are the pinnacle of gifts. God has many gifts: gifts that encompass the disbeliever and the believer, and encompass the obedient and the disobedient, and gifts specific to those who believe in Him; and these are the gifts of divinity to whoever hears the speech of his Lord in "do" and "do not do". His giving extends from creation to a sip of water, to a meal, to clothing, and to a dwelling, and every gift has a lifespan, and a gift's worth for a person rises with the lifespan of the gift; so every gift whose lifespan is extended is the happy gift.

If the gift of lordship (rububiyyah) relates to the provisions of matter and the sustenance of life, then the gifts of the Qur'an encompass this world and the Hereafter. And if what spoils any gift of this world is that a person parts from it by death, or that this gift withers in itself, then the gift of the Qur'an does not perish in this world or the Hereafter. We know that the Hereafter has no end, unlike this world, in which your life is not measured by its lifespan but by the appointed term set for you in it. And if the gifts of the Qur'an safeguard the values that bestow upon you the gifts of life that do not perish, namely the Hereafter life, then this is the loftiest gift; so beware of longing for a temporary blessing in the hands of anyone among them, from the blessings of the perishing world; for whoever has been given the Qur'an and thinks that another has been given something better than it has belittled what God has made great.

The expansion of the eye: it is the stretching and extending of a thing. The eye has ranges within which it sees what is seen; each eye according to its capacity. There are those who enjoy a strong and sharp sight, and there are those who do not. People vary in the ability of their sight according to a description set by physicians, so that they may treat it to the extent of their scientific capability. In everyday usage we hear someone say, "So-and-so has foresight" (ba'd nazar), meaning he possesses the ability to gauge reactions and anticipate what will happen and what results will follow from any action.

The intended meaning of "stretching the eye" is not taking out the eyeball and stretching it. Rather, what is meant is the continuation of gazing and close examination. But the Almighty expressed this in the Qur'an in this way, as if a person would take out the pupil of his eye to run with it and to look intently. This is what is understood from the wording of the verse, and the wording points to the intended meaning; and this is the very essence of the miraculous nature (i'jaz). The word "mata'" (enjoyment) indicates that something is enjoyed and then comes to an end; for this reason, the enjoyment of worldly life is described in the Qur'an as "the enjoyment of delusion" (mata' al-ghurur), that is, an enjoyment limited to a moment. The words of the Almighty: ﴿azwājan minhum﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 88), "zawj" is plural, and we have previously clarified that the word "zawj" is singular; when the male and the female come together, their name becomes "zawjayn" (a pair). The Almighty is the One who says: ﴿Glory be to the One who created all the pairs﴾ (Surah Ya-Sin, 36), and "all the pairs" means the single one, together with its counterpart from every kind of category. The intended meaning of the word "azwaj" here is that the opponents of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were in groups of groups: one misguided and one who misleads; and another misguided one with him who misleads. On the moment of reckoning, each of them will say: ﴿A speaker among them will say, "Indeed, I had a companion"﴾ (Surah As-Saffat, 51). Thus the word "azwaj" indicates various categories of those who stand in opposition to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and deny his methodology. In another place in the Qur'an, the Almighty reveals those whom the devils have led astray, and the Almighty gathers them with the devils in the Fire of Hell: ﴿And the Day He will gather them all, [and say], "O company of jinn, you have taken much from mankind"﴾ (Surah Al-An'am, 128). That is: O company of jinn, you have been able to inspire many of mankind with error and disobedience, so that they become your allies. Thus we find that every group that agrees upon something we call "azwaj." Here the Almighty clarifies: beware lest you extend your eyes toward what We have given enjoyment to some of them as pairs, for We have given you the highest gift, which is the miracle of the Qur'an, the guardian of values, which embraces the straight path. The Almighty continues: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾ (Surah Al-Hijr, 88).

It is said: "I grieved from him," "I grieved over him," and "I grieved for him." So if someone is struck by something that causes grief, and this cause did not originate from you, you say to him, "I grieve for you." And someone who commits an act that harms himself, you grieve over him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved over them, for he loved that they would believe and enjoy the blessing with which he himself was enjoying. For this reason, we find the Almighty saying about His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves; grievous to him is what you suffer, concerned over you, to the believers kind and merciful﴾ (Surah At-Tawbah, 128). From his compassion (ﷺ) it was difficult for him that his people should suffer hardship; compassion and mercy have their source in what Allah bestowed upon him of understanding the value of the blessing of faith. In another verse the Almighty says to His Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿Then perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their footsteps if they do not believe in this message, in sorrow﴾ (Surah Al-Kahf, 6). That is: nothing will be diminished from you if they do not believe, and their belief will not increase your reward; for upon you is only the conveyance. So why do you grieve over their not believing? The words of the Almighty here: ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾ (Surah Al-Hijr, 88) are evidence that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was eager that his people believe, out of love for them, and that they would come to know the sweetness of faith in Allah. The Prophet (ﷺ) would suffer and be pained in himself by their non-belief,

We know that the messengers are bringers of good news and warners. And one may ask: why does the form of warning always come first? I say: whoever believes is the one who receives the good news; as for the one who must expect the warning, he is the disbelieving denier. In warning there is a frightening of something that will befall you in the future; you must prepare for it so that you keep yourself away from being in it. Good news, however, concerns something the soul longs for. Through warning and good news, the situation becomes clear and plain, the human being is encompassed by all the matters of life, and the course of every affair becomes evident.

Thus, in the two preceding verses, the Truthful One (subhanahu) has bestowed His favour upon His Messenger (ﷺ) by giving him the seven oft-repeated verses and the Mighty Qur'an. Therefore He instructs him not to let his soul aspire to what some of the disbelievers have been given of rank and wealth, for the Qur'an is the honour of this world and the Hereafter.

He also instructs him not to grieve over them because of their turning away from his call, for he is only responsible for conveying the message. And he (ﷺ) should be humble toward the believers so that their attachment to him increases, for they are better than all the disbelievers in his message (ﷺ). Then the Truthful One (subhanahu) instructs him to make it known to all that he is a warner and a bringer of good news, clarifying what has come in the Qur'an of goodness that encompasses the believers and of punishment that descends upon the disbelievers. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of me and of what Allah has sent me with is like a man who came to a people and said: 'O people, I have seen the army with my own eyes, and I am the bare-chested warner, so hasten, hasten!' A group of his people obeyed him, set out in the night and proceeded at leisure, and so they were saved. But another group denied him, so they stayed in their place in the morning, and the army attacked them at dawn, destroyed them and annihilated them. That is the likeness of one who obeys me and follows what I have brought, and the likeness of one who disobeys me and denies the truth I have brought."

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 15, verse 90:

We know that He, glorified is He, sent down His Book upon His Messenger (ﷺ), and people received it in two ways. Some of them listened to the Qur'an, perceived the word of truth, and believed. Concerning these, the Truthful One, glorified is He, said: ﴿And when they hear what has been sent down to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so write us among the witnesses."﴾ (Surah al-Ma'idah 5:83). The other category listened to the Qur'an, but their hearts were like stones. Concerning them the Truthful One, glorified is He, said: ﴿And among them are those who listen to you, until, when they leave your presence, they say to those who were given knowledge, "What did he just say?" Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, and they follow their desires.﴾ (Surah Muhammad 47:16).

That is because their hearts are filled with disbelief, and they came in with a prior judgment, so they did not set up the scale of justice to weigh the benefit of what they hear. For this reason, the Truthful One, glorified is He, made clear to His Messenger (ﷺ) that he should not grieve. The matter has precedents with other messengers before you: every messenger came with a Book bearing the method, but people received those Books just as your people received what was sent down to you, dividing between disbeliever and believer, and they differed over matters concerning the Books sent down to their messengers.

Their division was like the division of your people concerning the Book sent down to you. So do not grieve if they accuse you of being a sorcerer, or that what has been sent down to you is poetry, or that you practise soothsaying; or they lost the ability to judge you and accused you of madness. Thus they divided the Qur'an sent down from Allah, glorified is He, into categories: sorcery, soothsaying, poetry, and madness, just as other peoples before them did. Some of them said, and the Qur'an recorded it against them: ﴿Indeed, your messenger who has been sent to you is mad.﴾ (Surah al-Shu'ara' 26:27).

Thus, O Messenger of Allah, you should know that you are not an innovation among the messengers, because messengers do not come to their peoples except when corruption and affliction have engulfed them. Corruption exists only when one party benefits from the corruption while harming others. When a messenger comes to reform this corruption, those who profit from it rise up to resist him and place obstacles in his way, just as happened to you, O Messenger of Allah, when some of them said: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it...﴾ (Surah Fussilat 41:26).

Such a statement indicates that if they had purified their souls and listened to the Qur'an, they would have been guided. Therefore their leaders say to them: ﴿...and talk noisily during it, so that you may overcome.﴾ (Surah Fussilat 41:26), meaning: create confusion around it. Thus the division with which the disbelievers received the Qur'an had already occurred with the messengers who came before you.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 15, verse 91:

The word ('idin) (عضين) means "pieces" or "parts." It is said of the butcher, when he slaughters a sheep or a calf, that he has made it ('idin), that is, he has separated each limb from the other, and likewise he has cut the thigh; that is, he has made the slaughtered animal into pieces after it had been connected limbs. Likewise, the Qur'an, when it was revealed, was one whole entity, and some of the disbelievers wanted to break it into parts. The intended here are a group of Jews and a group of Christians who were in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they wanted to divide the Qur'an as they had done with the two Books that were revealed to Musa (Moses), namely the Torah, and the Gospel that 'Isa (Jesus) brought. And the Truthful, glorified is He, said about them: ﴿And they have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾ [5:13] (Surat al-Ma'idah).

That is: some of the Jews have forgotten some of the Torah, and likewise some of the followers of 'Isa have forgotten some of the Gospel that was revealed to him. And even if we find them an excuse for forgetting, what about what they concealed of those books? What about what they altered and distorted of the words of those books? What about what they added to it, which was not sent down from Allah? All of this Allah, glorified is He, has exposed in the Qur'an. Or: the Jews received the Qur'an in the manner of one who accepts what does not burden them of it, and denied the part that burdens them; for example, they denied that their book had given good news of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Thus we see how they tried to make the Qur'an ('idin), that is, pieces separated from one another, and they tried this after it became clear to them that the Qur'an is influential and effective. And Allah, the Truthful, willed that the Qur'an should carry warning and good news. So the Messenger is a warner with the Qur'an, the clear and evident, to those who divided the matter concerning Muhammad (ﷺ): a group of them dedicated themselves to mocking Muhammad and those who believed with him; another group divided themselves to sit at the gates of Makkah during the season of Hajj, receiving those who came for Hajj from the various lands, to warn them against listening to Muhammad (ﷺ). Among these were those who described the Messenger (ﷺ) as a madman; among them were those who described the Qur'an as poetry; and among them were those who described the Messenger as a sorcerer.

Here the Truth, glory be to Him, swears by the attribute of Lordship (ar-Rububiyyah), by which He nurtured and cared for His Messenger, preparing him to be fit for the message, that He will not hand him over to anyone. It is He, glory be to Him, who said: ﴿And that you may be brought up under My eye﴾ (Surah Ta-Ha, 39), meaning that every messenger is fashioned and protected by His will, glory be to Him. That is the special protection of the methodology (al-manhajiyyah al-khassah), and the care of the chosen ones (al-mustafeen) who carry His message to creation. He, glory be to Him, has provided for all His creatures, and the Messengers come only for the task of conveying the methodology that governs the movement of life; therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, must provide them with a special kind of care. The words of the Truth, glory be to Him, here: ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ (Surah al-Hijr) show us that He, glory be to Him, will question them about the most minute details, and merely directing the question at them contains a kind of punishment.

Some who wish to find a contradiction in the Qur'an say: How does God say once: ﴿So that day no one will be questioned about his sin, neither man nor jinn﴾ (Surah ar-Rahman, 39), while in more than one place in the Qur'an He says that He will question these deniers? How can questioning be affirmed once and negated another time? We say to them: You approach the Qur'an with great superficiality. What you claim to be a contradiction is merely the outward appearance of the matter and not a contradiction in its reality. We know that any question has two purposes. The first purpose: that you learn what you do not know. The second purpose: that you acknowledge what you know. When the Truth, glory be to Him, negates a question, He negates that anyone will inform Him of what He does not know, glory be to Him; and when He affirms the question, this means that He will ask them a question of acknowledgment (su'al al-iqrar). Thus we know that when the Qur'an affirms an event once and negates it another time, then know that the aspect is separate (al-jihah munfakkah), i.e., the aspect of negation is other than the aspect of affirmation, and each of them has a different meaning. His words here:

﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ (Surah al-Hijr) mean that the one who strays and the one who leads astray, the follower and the one followed, will all be questioned about what they did.

The act, as we know, is the directing of a bodily organ toward its object. The object of the eye is to see; the object of the tongue is to speak; and the hand either strokes or seizes. Thus everything that the faculties of perception in the human soul produce, we call an act. We have already learned that action is divided into speech and deed. The Truth, glory be to Him, says:

﴿And Allah is not unaware of what you do.﴾ (Surah al-Baqarah) 

That is: remember that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, is not absent from anything, that everything you do He knows, and that you will meet Him on the Day of Resurrection, needing His mercy and His forgiveness.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 15, verse 94:

Meaning: Carry out your mission. Al-sad' (cleaving, splitting) means to make a crack in something solid and cohesive, just as we split glass with a special cutting tool, or as we make a breach in a wall. The Messenger (ﷺ) came to split disbelief and to demolish the strong, cohesive corruption that was sustained by the power of the chieftains of Quraysh. This term "al-sudah" (a splitting, a cracking) has become common in reference to glass, because it is difficult for a person to gather the fragments and small pieces that result from breaking it. Likewise, faith came to split the solid structure of disbelief and corruption.

The words of the Almighty: ﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 15:94). That is: give them the cold shoulder, and do not concern yourself with them. They will never submit to you, because they benefit from the corruption that you came to demolish. But they will come to you one after another, once your call has been firmly established and their hearts have come to be certain that what you brought is the truth. The example of this is the Islam of Khalid ibn al-Walid and 'Amr ibn al-'As, for they both said: "The matter has become settled for Muhammad, and our opposition to him no longer benefits anyone," and they entered Islam.

Following his words to him: ﴿And turn away from those who associate others with Allah.﴾ (Surah al-Hijr 15:94).

After it had been established for everyone who lived through that period that every mocker of Muhammad (ﷺ) had been struck by a punishment from the heavens: there was al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who strutted in his garments and walked over a piece of iron. He disdained to bend down to free his garment, which had caught on the piece of iron, so his foot was cut and was afflicted with gangrene, and they amputated it for him; then the gangrene spread through his whole body until he died. And there was the second, al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth, who was afflicted with a disease in his eyes and was struck with blindness; likewise al-Harith ibn al-Talatila, and al-As ibn Wa'il.

Every mocker of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was struck by some punishment, and whoever was not afflicted by a calamity or disease was felled by the swords of the Muslims at Badr, to such an extent that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) specified the places where each of the chieftains of Quraysh would meet his end; he said: "Here is the place of the death of so-and-so, and there is the place of the death of so-and-so." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicated those places before the battle began, and we know that war requires advance and retreat, yet what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had foretold happened exactly as he said.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 15, verse 96:

That is: these polytheists who mock you (ﷺ) will receive their punishment, because they associated partners with Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala). When the Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala) says: ﴿So they will come to know.﴾ (Surat al-Hijr, 15:96), this statement encompasses all times. That is, they will know now and after now, for the word "sawfa" (soon/later, a future particle) extends to all stages. Allah (subhanahu wa ta'ala) did not seize them all in one stage, but seized them over periods. When the extremist in harm is seized, some who harm may be deterred and retreat from continuing to harm, and some of them may turn to faith; the one whose severity was against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will find that same severity turned on the side of the Messenger (ﷺ).

The example is clear in Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl: he was struck at the Battle of al-Yarmuk, so he placed his head on the thigh of Khalid ibn al-Walid and asked: "O Khalid, is this a death that will make the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pleased with me?" Khalid replied: "Yes." So he surrendered his soul content. As for these mockers, they associated partners with Allah, so the gods they had associated with Allah did not benefit them in anything, and when that becomes certain to them, they become certain of the truth of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in what he conveyed from the Truth (subhanahu wa ta'ala).

In this noble statement, the Truth (al-Haqq), glorified is He, displays His appreciation for the feelings of prophethood. The Truth requires him to do such-and-such, and He, glorified is He, also knows what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) suffers in carrying out the commands of the Truth, glorified is He. This meaning also occurs in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿We know indeed that what they say grieves you; but it is not you they deny, rather it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 33). So you, O Messenger of Allah, are too noble to be a liar, for they testified to your good truthfulness through their living with you before the prophethood. And here He, glorified is He, says: ﴿And We certainly know that your breast is distressed by what they say﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 97).

The meaning of constriction of the breast (ḍīq al-ṣadr) is that the air entering the lungs through the process of breathing decreases; from this air the lungs extract the oxygen and expel carbon dioxide; and oxygen works to oxidise food to produce energy. If the chest is constricted, the energy becomes little. The example becomes clear to those who climb the high staircase of any house or any place and find themselves panting (yanhajūn); the reason for this panting is that the lung wants to hasten to take in a larger quantity of air than what reaches it, so the heart works more intensely so as to enable the lung to draw in a greater quantity of air.

As for one whose chest is broad, he draws in as much air as he wishes, which enables the lung to take the quantity it needs of air, so the person of the broad chest does not pant. Thus, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was denied by someone, or mocked by someone, his chest would be constricted, and the quantity of air necessary for movement would be constricted; therefore the Truth, glorified is He, reassures him that His supply to him does not end. You notice the process of constriction of the chest in yourself when someone irritates you and you lash out at him; then he says to you: "Why is your chest constricted? Broaden your chest a little." And the Truth, glorified is He, says in another place:

﴿So whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 125), i.e., He widens his breast, and his capacity to understand the meanings that the upright religion came with increases. And He also says: ﴿And whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing into the sky…﴾ (Surah al-An'am, 125).

Here we find that the Truth, glorified is He, explains the process of ascent as though it involves striving and toil, and this contradicts the well-known matter that when you ascend higher you find the air purer. It has been established that the higher a person climbs into the atmosphere, the less air he will find.

He (ﷺ) is taught Allah's remedy for the constriction of the breast that comes when a denier or a mocker grieves or hurts him: "We know that your breast is constricted by what they say. So glorify your Lord with praise and be among those who prostrate."

In the same way, any constriction can be dispelled for you by glorifying Allah (tasbih). If people turn away from you or creatures trouble you, know that you are able to find intimacy with Allah through tasbih. You will find no one more merciful than Him, and when you glorify your Lord you declare Him free of every imperfection and praise Him, so that you live under the shelter of His mercy. For this reason we find Him saying in another place:

﴿So had he not been one of those who glorify Allah, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ (Surat al-Saffat)

Therefore, when your breast is constricted by worldly causes, turn to the Causer (al-Musabbib). We always join tasbih with hamd (praise). Tanzih (declaring Allah free of imperfection) applies to His essence, His attributes, and His acts. He is perfect in His essence, His attributes, and His acts. His essence resembles no essence, His attributes are eternal and absolute, while the attributes of creation are a gift from Him and originated. The acts of the Truth are subject to no judge except His will, glory be to Him. For this reason, He, may He be exalted, says regarding tasbih:

﴿Glory be to the One who created all the pairs.﴾ (Surat Ya-Sin)

He also says:

﴿So glorify Allah when you enter the evening and when you enter the morning.﴾ (Surat al-Rum)

Both evening and morning are signs from Him. When the sun sets, that is a permission for rest; when the sun rises, that is a permission to set out to work. The glorification of the creature of the Creator is something in which none of His creatures ever shares with Allah. So the solace of the believer, when the causes of life constrict him, is to turn to his Lord away from the harshness of creatures, so as to find psychological rest, for he takes refuge in a mighty pillar. Some of the gnostics of Allah (al-ʿarifun billah), explaining this matter, sought to give the believing soul consolation for the coldness of people toward it, and they say: "If He has made you lonely with His creation, know that He wants to make you intimate with Himself."

When you glorify Allah, you acknowledge that His essence is not like your essence, His attributes are not like your attributes, and His acts are not like your acts, and all of that is for your own benefit. Your power and the power of other humans is a power of weakness and change, whereas His power is inherent in Him, absolute and eternal, and He is the One who brings you every blessing. Therefore you must accompany tanzih with hamd: you praise your Lord because He is free of being like you, and praise of Allah is obligatory at all times. He, glory be to Him, created all gifts to serve you. When you see a person of talent and envy him for it, and you praise Allah that He has granted him that talent, the good of that blessing reaches you. When you glorify Allah with His praise, He does not break His promise to you of all good, for all of us may break promises despite ourselves, because we are changeable, whereas He never breaks His promise. For this reason blessing overwhelms you whenever you glorify and praise Allah. Increase in submission to the Benefactor, and prostrate in obedience to His command, may He be exalted:

﴿And be among those who prostrate.﴾ (Surat al-Hijr)

Prostration is the broadest manifestation of submission, and the human face, as we know, is what displays dignity, by which one meets people, and it is the first thing one protects from anything that soils it or diminishes your satisfaction with it. Whoever prostrates with the best of what is in him, this is a submission that gives honor. Whoever submits to Allah in gratitude for His blessings, He gives him of honor what suffices him from every aspect of prostration. We all remember the words of the poet:

"And the prostration you dislike in it, out of a thousand prostrations, is salvation."

Prostration is the summit of submission to the Truth, glory be to Him. Humans dislike the word "servitude" (ʿubudiyyah), because human history has carried many injustices as a result of humans serving humans. This kind of servitude, as we know, gives the servant's benefit to the master, but servitude to Allah gives His benefit, glory be to Him, to the servants, and in that is the highest honoring of the human being.

The worship (ʿibadah) is known to be the obedience of the worshipper to the commands of the one worshipped, whether by way of enjoining or prohibiting, and the application of "do" and "do not." Many people think that worship consists only of the outward matters of the five pillars: the testimony that there is no god but God, the establishment of prayer, the giving of zakat, the fasting of Ramadan, and the pilgrimage to the House for whoever is able to make his way to it. We say: No. These are the foundations upon which worship stands. That is, they are the structure upon which the rest of worship rests. Thus worship becomes: everything without which an obligation cannot be fulfilled is itself obligatory. That is, the whole movement of life, even sweeping the streets and removing harm from the road, is worship. Everything intended to benefit people is worship, so that Muslims do not become a burden on others.

In the establishment of the pillars there is a display of the strength of the Muslims, when they show complete loyalty to God by performing prayer five times a day. The Muslim leaves his work the moment he hears the call "Allahu akbar," and so he steps out of the struggles of life and declares his loyalty to the Creator, the Bestower of blessings. When the Muslim fasts a month in the year, he declares his loyalty to the Most Generous Creator, and he abstains from many things that were permitted to him. As soon as the time of abstention approaches, shortly before the dawn prayer, he immediately refrains. This compliance with the commands of the Truth, glorified is He, reminds you of His blessings upon you. In your ordinary day you do not approach the prohibited things, which took time during the early days of the religion until Muslims abstained from them. So no Muslim thinks of drinking wine, and none of them thinks of gambling. Those matters have become imprinted and have turned into a behavioural habit, carried out with familiarity and routine by the majority of Muslims who implement the Shariah of God and apply "do" and "do not."

When fasting comes, you abstain from things that are lawful to you the whole year, and you spend any day of Ramadan with your soul awaiting the sound of the call to the sunset prayer so that you may break your fast. Thus you comply with the command to abstain and the command to break the fast, and this trains you in many acts of obedience that become a habit for believers. God, glorified is He, wishes to give you a taste of the pleasure of religious obligation. Some people go astray when they interpret, according to their own desires, His word, the Truth:

﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾ (Surah al-Hijr, 99).

One of these people says, deceiving others, "I have reached the rank of certainty," and he refrains from performing the obligations of prayer, fasting, zakat, and the pilgrimage to the Sacred House, although he is able, and claims that the obligation has fallen from him because certainty has reached him. We say to whoever claims this: Do you deceive God and His Messenger? We all know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued to perform the obligatory duties until the last day of his life. And we all know that the certainty agreed upon, which all humanity holds and about which there is absolutely no dispute, is death. As for certainty regarding the unseen, it is among the special qualities of the believer; once its matter reaches him from the Qur'an, he affirms it and does not ask how its matter comes about. The clear example is Abu Bakr al-Siddiq: when they would tell him of some strange matter from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would say, "If he has said it, then he has spoken the truth."

As for the disbeliever, God forbid, he doubts everything unseen, or even material, unless it is perceptible to him. But as soon as death comes to him, he knows that it is the only certainty. For this reason we find ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz saying: "I have never seen a certainty more like doubt than people's certainty about death." We all are certain that we will die, yet we push this certainty far away from us, although it is an event that will inevitably occur. When death comes, we say: this is the moment in which nothing benefits except a person's deeds, if he was a believer fulfilling the rights of God. Therefore I always say: certainty is the affirmation of a matter with firm confirmation, such that it does not surface in the mind to be debated again, after you have learned it from sources whose truthfulness you trust in what they convey to you.

As for the eye of certainty, it is that which sees the event and so becomes certain of it, or it is a real matter that enters your heart so that you affirm it. Thus certainty has stages: a matter that you affirm with decisive affirmation, so that it does not surface in the mind to be debated again, and for which there are sources of knowledge from someone whose truthfulness you trust; or the consensus of people who never agree upon falsehood. This is "knowledge of certainty" (ʿilm al-yaqin). If you see the matter with your own eyes, this is "eye of certainty" (ʿayn al-yaqin)... and the believer bases his affirmation and certainty on what has reached him from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Behold, the Imam ʿAli, may God ennoble his face and be pleased with him, says: "Even if the veil were lifted from the unseen matters that the Messenger of God told us, I would not gain any more certainty." And behold, our master Harithah, may God be pleased with him, says: "It is as if I am looking at the people of Paradise in Paradise enjoying bliss, and at the people of the Fire being tormented." The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: "You have known, so hold fast to it." That is certainty as the Companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, believed in it.
